About
Even if you have never sailed or paddled before, Funcat's friendly and experienced staff will have you out on the water in no time. After some basic tuition and demonstration, you will be out sailing on the beautiful swan river before you know it. Our Hobie cats up to four people, so those nobody will miss out on any of the fun. For the more experienced sailor you may enjoy the perfect racing arena that is found on the Swan.
Age Recommendations and Rules
Q. At what age is it safe to take children on a catamaran?
A. 5 years of age is the youngest age we will allow children on the catamarans. If you wish to take young children on a catamaran, we suggest that you discuss this with us on the day. Factors such as sailing experience of the person in charge of the catamaran and the conditions on the day very much influence the advice we give to hirers.
Someone 16 or over MUST be present on each boat in your hire. If you do not have a 16-year-old or older present, unfortunately your booking will be forfeit.

Beginner Surfing Lessons with all equipment!
Rates
A$40 per person
The Lesson:
GO Surf School will teach you the skills of surfing and how to handle yourself and your surfboard in the ocean, while having a stack of fun along the way. Beginner and Intermediate surfers will also learn how to assess surf conditions and identify potential risks. We provide coaching to all ages and levels of surfing ability. Our instructors are there to help you learn to surf and provide advice on all questions related to surfing. We hope that you’ll love surfing as much as we do. We'll get you up and riding in no time!
What to Expect:
Roll up at the beach at your start time with your swimwear on.
Your coach will introduce themselves and gets you sorted with a wetsuit and board.
You will start with some beach-based technique and surf safety info. We are big on getting it right on the beach and getting you ready to hit the waves.
You then hit the surf in waist deep water and waves suitable for your ability.
Surf coaches will help get you up and riding by pushing you into a few waves, giving feedback on your technique, keeping an eye on your safety, encouraging you and maximising your fun.
Surfers will leave the water approximately 15mins prior to the end of the lesson.
A feedback session with goals for your next surf lesson is done before getting changed.
What is provided:
All equipment is provided including surfboards suited to your abilities. Our equipment is the best available on the market and produced specifically for surf schools. We use soft, stable boards that are easy to balance, paddle, stand and surf on for intermediate and beginner surfers. Quality Rip Curl and Quiksilver wetsuits keep you warm and coloured GO Surf School rash vests easily identify you in the water.
What to bring:
Surfers need to wear a swimsuit or boardies and bring a towel and lots of sunscreen. Don’t forget a camera to document the fun you will have.

WHAT IS HIGH PERFORMANCE ALL ABOUT?
Our high performance coaching camps are about reaching your true surfing ability with the help of a few clever strategies, delivered by our highly qualified, professional and friendly coaches.
WHAT STRATEGIES DO YOU USE?
Video Analysis: We use video analysis to improve your surfing technique and skill level. Our high performance coaches film your surfing session from the beach, then sit with you to go over your footage in detail and give you constructive feedback on your strengths and areas in need of improvement. You then get to go back out in the water to put the advice in to practice. You will be amazed at how the slightest tweak can make you look and feel like a whole new and improved surfer!
Surf Skates: No wave is ever the same and conditions are forever changing. Practice makes improvements and getting the feel of how your body should be balanced and positioned is really important to nailing those turns you have always dreamed of! Our surf skates are purpose built to create the same feeling of surfing and let you repeatedly practice a manoeuvre (on land) with our high performance coaches right there giving instant feedback.
Competition Practice: This is optional for those participants who are competition surfers. If requested, we can hold mock competitions and run through successful heat strategies to improve your confidence and technique to be ready for your next comp.

Nestled between New Zealand’s highest mountains, the Tasman Sea, stunning temperate rainforest, glowing glaciers, mirror lakes and braided river beds, Franz Josef Glacier has been described as one of the most beautiful place on earth. Discover an unforgettable Aoraki/Mount Cook glacier adventure combining a ski plane flight and a helicopter experience in one day. Soar up the Tasman Valley with incredible views of Tasman Terminal Lake, the Hochstetter Icefall, Grand Plateau, and the towering peak of Aoraki/Mount Cook before landing on the upper snowfields of the Tasman Glacier.
Step out onto the snow as the aircraft fully shuts down, allowing you to enjoy the silence, crisp alpine air, and year-round snow and ice. After time for photos and exploration, swap aircraft and return to Mount Cook Airport with sweeping views of the full length of the Tasman Glacier.

Monkey Mia Marine Life Cruise 2 – 1:30 PM to 3:30 PM
This cruise is offered only during the Western Australia School Holidays and opens for booking once our Morning Cruise (10:00 AM – 12:30 PM) is nearing capacity. A minimum of 10 adults is required to operate this cruise.
About
Step aboard the spectacular 18-metre sailing catamaran, Aristocat 2, for a cruise through nature’s aquarium in search of dugongs, sponging dolphins, loggerhead and green turtles, manta rays, and other amazing and endangered marine life. The experience also includes an energising salt spa in the boom net, with multiple vantage points to enjoy the stunning surroundings.
We are the only cruise operator licensed to interact with marine life in the Exclusion Zone . This means as soon as we leave the jetty, we can stop at any time to take full advantage of your marine life sighting experience. We will go in search of marine life including dolphins, dugongs, turtles, rays, and sharks from the moment we leave the jetty.
Boom netting is available on this cruise.
Viewing vantage points around the entire boat
All-weather outdoor & indoor seating
Boom net (bring your bathers and towel)
Indoor fully licensed Ocean Lounge Bar
Wheelchair access throughout the boat
Wheelchair-accessible toilet
Marine Life Experience
While we strive to spot wild animals on our Marine Life Cruises, sightings cannot be guaranteed. Our skipper and crew have many years of experience in Shark Bay and will always do their best to find animals for you to observe. Sightings may vary seasonally; dugong season runs from August to May.
meta_raw_booking_notes:
#Cruise Information
#**Please meet at the Monkey Mia Jetty 15 minutes prior to departure for your Monkey Mia Marine Life Cruise** 
Monkey Mia is 25 kilometres from the town of Denham, about a 20 minute drive.

**Dress Code**
We suggest bringing camera, sunscreen and sunglasses, as well as bathers and a towel if you wish to join in the ocean salt spa/boom netting at the back of the boat.
Please bring a jumper or jacket during the winter months as the breeze across the Bay can be quite chilly at times.

**Passenger Information**
Drinks and snacks are available for purchase on board including beer, wine, champagne, soft drinks, juice, tea, coffee & water, chips and muesli bars. We also allow BYO drinks and snacks.

**Monkey Mia Conservation Reserve Fee**
There is a fee payable to Parks and Wildlife Service to enter the Monkey Mia area. However if you are planning to to be in Monkey Mia for our cruise only that fee is waived. Your arrival should be no more than half and hour before the cruise boarding time and leaving straight after the cruise. Please show proof of booking to the Service staff at the Monkey Mia gate or at the shop on the foreshore.

**Marine Life Experience**
As we endeavour to look at wild animals while on our Marine Life Cruises there is no guarantee that we will sight animals during the cruise. The skipper and crew have many years of experience in Shark Bay and will always try their hardest to find animals for you to look at. Unfortunately due to seasonal changes our sightings will vary. Dugong season is August - May. Dugong sightings are more challenging in winter months 

**Supervision of Children**
As a responsible tour boat operator it is essential to ensure the safety and comfort of all passengers onboard. Unfortunately there are times when unsupervised children pose a risk to themselves and others, especially on a boat where there are many potential hazards. If parents or guardians have been warned about lack of supervision of their children and there is no change to the behaviour, we will return to the jetty for that family to disembark. No refund for the cruise will be offered in these circumstances. We hope you understand and respect the decision of the skipper

**Weather Information**
All activities and cruises are subject to weather conditions and at the skipper’s discretion.
Please remember, we cannot control the weather. We still run cruises on windy, overcast and rainy days. We always advise to check the weather before your cruise date.

##Precis of Queensland cycling rules and safety
RULES
PATHWAYS
Shared pathways
	•	Keep Left, ring bell to warn of passing pedestrians
	•	Cyclists give way to people, slow down
Separate pathways
	•	Cyclists use the side of the pathway indicated by the sign
Bicycle only
	•	For bicycles only
	•	You can use any speed
On-road bicycle lanes.
	•	You must follow all road rules
	•	You are sharing the road with other vehicles
	•	Keep as far left as possible
NO Bicycle zone
	•	You must dismount and walk your bike
DO NOT RIDE IN PUBLIC SQUARES, WALK YOUR BIKE.
RIDING
	•	Keep at two hands on handlebars unless giving signals.
	•	Have one leg on each side of the seat.
	•	Face forward.
	•	To signal RIGHT-TURN, extend arm out horizontally with hand open, palm facing forward. To signal STOP, raise arm with elbow bent at right angle and hand up with palm facing forward.
	•	One person per bike unless the bike is designed as a tandem bike.
	•	Keep two meters from the back of a vehicle when following.
	•	DO NOT ride into the path of a driver or pedestrian.
	•	Keep left at all times.
	•	Do not overtake another vehicle on the left if that vehicle is indicating and turning left.
	•	Do not ride more than two abreast.
	•	If riding beside another rider, ride no more than 1.5m apart.
For a more comprehensive list of rules go to https://www.qld.gov.au/transport/safety/rules/wheeled-devices/bicycle 
IF YOU BREAK THE ROAD RULES YOU MAY BE FINED. THERE IS NO AGE LIMIT FOR BEING FINED.
SAFETY
	•	Wear your helmet and enclosed shoes
	•	Cycle at appropriate speed. 
	•	Go slow when there are people about.
	•	Ring the bell when approaching pedestrians, dogs, etc.
	•	Keep left at all times.
	•	Use appropriate lights and reflectors in low light level situations and at night.

SAIL
We provide catamaran sailing cruises on Darwin Harbour.
Our specially designed tourism catamaran Kuru, provides an enjoyable way to experience Darwin harbour. This unique harbour experience allows you to sit back and enjoy cool sea breezes, precious time with family, friends, work colleagues and your work clients.
Some on the harbour say they sail, we actually do! Our harbour route is governed by the wind as well as the strong tides experienced in the harbour. Obviously, if there is no wind we cannot sail. On our return sail/cruise to Cullen Bay guests will be able to view the city lights and our crew can point out interesting planets and constellations visible in the night sky.

You can enjoy our nibbles plates along with a tasty marinated Asian themed BBQ and salad meal with an to option BYO drinks or try our catered package of bubbles, free red or white wine and mid strength beer.

#To save your valuable holiday time or time from your ABC Reef Reef Safari please complete the Pre Arrival Waiver which will be sent to you shortly. 

---

##Important Information: 

**Medical info:** 
While certified divers are required to fill out the medical form on-board as well, their certification status allows them a bit more leeway in determining their medical fitness to dive. Certified divers (divers with a licence) generally need to be able to answer the following questions: 

- Since completing your last dive medical assessment, have you suffered any illness or injury that may affect your ability to dive safely? 
- Are you currently suffering any illness or injury? 
- Are you currently taking any prescription medication, other than the contraceptive pill? 

Certified divers are generally allowed to dive if they can answer “no” to the first two questions. If they are taking prescription medication, they are generally okay to dive if they were taking it while they were doing their course or have had an updated medical. 

Example if you have not dived for a few years and you are taking medication **(especially if it is for anxiety, high blood pressure or anything else relating to heart /lungs)** you would not be able to scuba dive in Queensland until a dive doctor has put in writing FIT TO DIVE. 

We cannot refund if it turns out on the dive day that you suffer from a condition incompatible with diving and you fail to bring a clear to dive confirmation from an accredited dive doctor. 

[View Australian Dive Doctors.pdf](https://cdn.filestackcontent.com/frW9Ab8aTwyWWpB0f1Zz)

**What to bring:** 
A towel, sunglasses, hat, swimmers and a change of clothes, dive log book and your certification card (if you are a certified diver). 

**Sunscreen:** 
Sunscreen is found to be damaging the reef, coral are very sensitive to chemical additives found in conventional sunscreen, which is why we recommend you to cover yourself with clothes. However, Reef and skin friendly sunscreen with no harmful additives is available at our shop. 

**Keep Warm & Protected:** 
If you suffer from the cold or prefer to have your own personal under garment, we have a variety at our shop. We provide: Good humour and all snorkel/dive equipment, lycra (stinger/rash guard suits) and or wet suits, buffet lunch, tea/coffee, fruit and cakes & water.

**Seasickness?**
If you are not sure prevention is better than cure. 
We recommend TRAVACALM (Pink&white box), a non drowsy medication available at most chemists in Australia. Take medication 1 hour before boat departure (otherwise medication won’t work). [Please read more about it here.](https://cdn.filestackcontent.com/1mPlz4jR0ajaS6pfIaXu)

**Meeting Location:** 
Please be at our boat at 7.45am INDEPENDENCE 1. Our boat is in a small private marina at Marano’s Fuel Station and is located on southern end of Wharf Street. There is FREE PARKING. There is an ABC Reef Safaris sign on the LEFT side of entrance and and a temporary sign for fuel prices on the RIGHT hand side.

10.00am-4.00pm timeslot - pick-up will be at **9.30am**  

11.00am-5.00pm timeslot - pick-up will be at **10.30am**  

#Being ready and raring to go for the shuttle 
You could be the first we come to collect, so if you can please be ready and waiting for the shuttle, that would be fabulous, as there will very likely be others needing to be picked up as well and we don’t want to keep them waiting long.  The shuttle will meet you out by the gate of your accommodation or at the main reception of your hotel/motel/campground 😊  For those of you who do find yourselves waiting, thank you for your patience, we promise we have not forgotten about you, and we are not far away. 

#What you need to bring
Credit cards for tasting charges, lunch and buying wine
Phone
Your “International Passport” or “NZ Drivers License” (only form of ID the cellar doors are legally able to accept)
Waterproof jacket, comfortable shoes
Bottle of water

#Cellar Doors
Your day is your own where you have the freedom to pick and choose who you want to visit 
but don't worry about doing too much planning in advance as we will be here to help you on the day with lots of up-to-date information about the cellar doors, as well as heaps of friendly advice about how you can make the most of your day, too. 😊 

There are upwards of 14+ beautiful cellar doors who are more than happy for you to visit them for a tasting without the need to book an appointment in advance, however, there are some exceptions to this rule:-
**Cloudy Bay** (a 40 minute bike ride from our base)
**Hunters** (a 40 minute bike ride from our base)
**Hans Herzog** (a 20 minute bike ride from our base)
**Framingham Wines** (a 10 minute bike ride from our base)

If any of these 4 cellar doors are on your bucket list, just head to their websites to find their booking forms.  With Cloudy Bay and Hunters being 40 minutes away, we would recommend you make a booking between 12 Noon -1pm so that you get the big bike ride out of the way at the start of the day when you are nice and fresh, then you can work your way back and be close to home at the end. 😊 

There are some cellar doors that we feel are too far away to get to on a bike, or that the roads to reach them are just not safe - Clos Henri, Saint Clair's, Wither Hills, Lawsons Dry Hills - we feel these are best visited by car.

For groups over 8+ pax - the cellar doors do ask that we book you in and we will work with you and help put together a personalized itinerary and get spots secured at the cellar doors for you.   

#Cheese & Mixed Platters
Most of the cellar doors have platter food available for purchase if you wish to have something to nibble on alongside your tastings.  These can be ordered when you arrive at the cellar door. 

#Restaurants 
**Bookings are recommended and we are always here to help if you are not sure what time to book😊**
**Vines Village Café** - 20 minutes biking from our base (Open 7 days a week).  
**The Fancy Cow** - 25 minutes biking from our base (Open 6 days, closed on Mondays) 
**Allan Scott** - 40 minutes biking from our base – bookings essential - (Open 7 days a week)
**Number 11 at Wairau River** - 15 minutes biking from our base - (Open 7 days a week as of 7th November 2024) 

Note: Wither Hills and Saint Clair’s restaurants are not accessible on our bikes - they are too far away and the roads are not safe getting to them - we feel they are best visited by car :-) 

#For those on the Roadsters
These bikes need to stay on the bike paths and quiet roads, so the beautiful cellar doors you can visit are...
**Gibson Bridge**
**Forrest Wines** - platters available for purchase
**Framingham Wines** - "build your own platter" - food available for purchase
**Nautilus Estate** - platter food available for purchase
**Bladen** - food truck & platters food available for purchase (closed on Wednesdays)
**Boomtown Beer Garden** - food truck (Open Thurs-Sun as of 1st November 2024)
**Number 11 at Wairau River** - restaurant and tasting room (Open 7 days a week as of 7th November 2024)  

#Tasting experience charges at the cellar doors 
These range from $16.00 p/p - $30.00 p/p at each cellar door and are not included in the bike hire rate.  These charges need to be paid by you directly to the cellar doors on the day, and they can accept Visa / Mastercard / Cash.

We are really looking forward to seeing you but if you have any questions before you arrive, please just ask away as we are always here to help :-)

Take care and we will see you soon.

Cheers
Lorelle and Greg

* Keep your balance on a rough track. You’ll be walking over loose rocks and gravel, 
   including going down a steep gravel slope with no handrail or stairs
* Take everything on the Day Hikes packing list including lots of warm and waterproof 
  clothes
* Cope with extreme weather, including rain and cold. The track is in an alpine environment.

Following this you will descend via a volcanic rock scree track to the Emerald Lakes (Ngarotopounamu), noted for their distinctive greenstone hue. After walking past Blue Lake also known as Te Wai-whakaata-o-te-Rangihiroa (Rangihiroa’s mirror), the track skirts the northern slopes of Tongariro eventually descending in a zigzag fashion to the road terminus at 760 metres.

Thanks for choosing your adventure with WAM! We can't wait for you to join us on a spectacular journey into nature.

Just by booking with us, you have done a lot of good for the planet, congratulations! (read on for more details of how)

Before we do so, please take a minute to read some important information about your tour:

- WAM Adventures require a minimum of 4 people to run. We almost always run our trips but we'll be in contact as we get closer to the date for updates.
- You’ll start receiving emails as we get closer to the date.
- Once you have a date confirmed, if you need to cancel, we require a minimum 7 days notice to provide a refund (please read our T&C's for other options) 

##Pick up Location
We meet on the Mornington Peninsula at Devilbend Natural Features Reserve, 159 Graydens Rd, Moorooduc VIC 3933. Please contact us if you would like to discuss an alternative pick up location on the Mornington Peninsula, or we can also pick up from Frankston Train Station.

##Gift vouchers
If you have a gift voucher, you'll need to redeem it at some stage by returning to the relevant tour page, selecting a date and entering the voucher code at the checkout - think of your voucher as like a pre-paid credit card
Also, we can’t extend the use-by date on gift vouchers past three years (three years is pretty good!)

##Premium Service
- We include everything you need on your adventure including activities, equipment, food and refreshments. 

- To maximise your comfort we even provide you with eco-pack for the day which includes some special products from local businesses that directly support the environment. This includes free sunscreen and a towel service. You simply hand these back at the end of your experience. Its a bit like a pack you may get on a first class flight or a luxury hotel, except ours is good for the planet!

##Now for the deep and meaningful:
By booking an adventure with us you have directly helped make a long-term positive environmental and social impact by:
- Planting native trees on the Mornington Peninsula with MP Koalas to capture carbon emissions, protect our climate, enhance soil and water quality, and restore habitat for native wildlife. 
- Regenerate reefs and native kelp locally with The Nature Conservancy, providing marine habitat, filtering seawater, removing nitrogen and phosphate, and preventing used shell from entering landfill.
- Support female education with The Stars Foundation which empowers and supports Indigenous young women and girls to complete education and find work.
- Protect and plant mangroves to protect our coastlines, wildlife and support blue carbon projects.

You'll find additional information relevant to your adventure on the Wild Adventures Melbourne website. Please check the website for exactly what items we recommend bringing with you on the day.

##Green is our Gold Commitment:

As members of Australia’s tourism industry, we believe a land as precious
as ours should be preserved for generations to come. As a visitor, we ask that you do the same. That’s why we’ve set some unwritten rules that have kept our backyard beautiful for thousands of years.

Passed down through story and practice, they’re how we walk gently, listen deeply, tread with care – and look out for each other along the way. 

By following them throughout your visit, you too can care for Australia when you Come and say G’day.

Consider these principles a bit of local knowledge. A few fundamentals to help you respect this place and have an unforgettable stay in the process.

The Guiding Principles:

Celebrate Community
The best part of an Australian visit is the people you meet.
Shop local, engage with communities, and you’ll leave with new mates aplenty.

Embrace Culture
Australia’s cultural diversity stretches from ancient songlines to city laneways. Immerse yourself in it all - honour First Nations cultures, embrace our diversity, and you’ll leave with new knowledge and new friends.

Preserve Place
In Australia you’ll find some of the most unspoilt landscapes on Earth. Help keep them that way by minimising your impact wherever you go.

Respect Wildlife
Australia has some of the most unique animals on the planet. Take as many photos as you like but remember to give them space and respect their homes.

Take Care
We look out for one another in Australia, but it’s important to take care of yourself too. Listen to the land, respect it, and always put safety first.


If you have any questions between now and your trip with us, please don't hesitate to email or call me directly.

Looking forward to adventuring with you soon,

Nic 'Coops' Cooper
WAM Founder

Ages
All Ages
120 - 150 Minutes
This is an ALL IN ONE cruise. Join us onboard our 50ft passenger vessel 'Asherah' and explore ALL our stunning bay and coastline has to offer.
Fowlers Bay is home to an abundance of endangered, vulnerable and protected species of marine mammals and oceanic bird life. Let us give you the opportunity to engage with some of Australia's iconic creatures including :
- Southern Right Whales
- Humpback Whales
- Common Dolphins
- Bottlenose Dolphins
- Australian Sea Lions
- New Zealand Fur Seals
- Little Penguins
- Albatross
- White Bellied Sea Eagles
In this interactive and informative cruise, you'll discover the fascinating yet brutal history of Fowlers Bay, learn about Whale Baleen Plate, hold some very rare Ambergris and listen to realtime underwater acoustics including the famous Humpback Whale Song!

Looking for safe activities to do with the family & friends? Get out into the fresh air and sea.
Rates
Person $250 (up to 2 people)
Extra Person $40
Duration
1.5 hours
Availability
Weekends (excluding January)
About
In light of the current COVID-19 situation Go Surf is now offering private group and family Surf lessons. You won’t be in with other people.
All equipment and wetsuits provided.
In accordance with current advice, Go Surf will ensure staff and participants exercise an extra high standard of cleanliness and personal hygiene and limit personal contact. All equipment is thoroughly disinfected between lessons. Your health is our number one priority.
You can choose to book a scheduled date and time available on our calendar
OR
go to Gift Cards and purchase open dated private lesson, then contact Go Surf to organise a suitable day and time of your choice (subject to staff availability and weather).
The Lesson:
GO Surf School will teach you the skills of surfing and how to handle yourself and your surfboard in the ocean, while having a stack of fun along the way. Beginner and Intermediate surfers will also learn how to assess surf conditions and identify potential risks. We provide coaching to all ages and levels of surfing ability. Our instructors are there to help you learn to surf and provide advice on all questions related to surfing. We hope that you’ll love surfing as much as we do. We'll get you up and riding in no time!
What to Expect:
Roll up at the beach at your start time with your swimwear on.
Your coach will introduce themselves and gets you sorted with a wetsuit and board.
You will start with some beach-based technique and surf safety info. We are big on getting it right on the beach and getting you ready to hit the waves.
You then hit the surf in waist deep water and waves suitable for your ability.
Surf coaches will help get you up and riding by pushing you into a few waves, giving feedback on your technique, keeping an eye on your safety, encouraging you and maximising your fun.
Surfers will leave the water approximately 15mins prior to the end of the lesson.
A feedback session with goals for your next surf lesson is done before getting changed.
What is provided:
All equipment is provided including surfboards suited to your abilities. Our equipment is the best available on the market and produced specifically for surf schools. We use soft, stable boards that are easy to balance, paddle, stand and surf on for intermediate and beginner surfers. Quality Rip Curl, Billabong and Quiksilver wetsuits keep you warm and coloured GO Surf School rash vests easily identify you in the water.
What to bring:
Surfers need to wear a swimsuit or boardies and bring a towel and lots of sunscreen. Don’t forget a camera to document the fun you will have.

Every woman is unique. This day is designed to celebrate your strength, your energy, and your connection to the ocean.
Whether you’re stepping onto a surfboard for the very first time or chasing your next wave with confidence, our Women’s Surf, Yoga & Wellness Day on the Gold Coast invites you to discover adventure, empowerment, and balance.
What You’ll Experience:
Surfing – Find Your Freedom
Choose your level:
Beginner Surf Lesson (Level 1): Learn the essentials — paddling, popup, stance, and riding waves with confidence.
Intermediate Surf Coaching (Level 2): Take your surfing further — catching unbroken waves, refining turns, and building speed with control.
Surf Yoga – Move & Breathe
Start your day with yoga by the sea. Gentle stretches, breathwork, and mindful movement to align body and mind before you hit the waves.
Surf Fitness – Build Strength & Flow
Functional training designed for surfers: mobility, balance, and core strength, helping you move better in the water and in everyday life.
Time to Connect & Reflect
Healthy snacks and a nourishing lunch give space to recharge, share stories, and soak in the Gold Coast lifestyle.
Why Join?
This is more than a surf lesson. It’s a day for women to explore adventure, challenge themselves, and reconnect with nature. Whether you’re local or living here on a temporary visa, this is your chance to feel part of a supportive community of women, united by the ocean.

7:00 am – Welcome & meet at location (Gold Coast, TBC with ocean conditions)

8:15 am – Surf lesson (choose Beginner or Intermediate)
10:15 am – Break & light snack
10:30 am – Surf fitness / mobility & breathwork session
11:30 am – Lunch & reflection
12:30 pm – Debrief & finish
What’s Included:
Surfboards & wetsuits
Yoga & fitness sessions
Healthy snacks & lunch
A supportive, empowering environment for women

##The day will be broken up into 3 parts; Surfing, Surf Fitness & Surf Yoga:

Step out into nature, feel the breeze of the ocean on your skin and your toes melting into the sand as you embark on your journey towards a healthier, fitter and more relaxed version of yourself with our Women Surf, Yoga & Wellness Day.

“Women Surf & Wellness Day “ looks at combining women’s passion for the ocean, adventure and being active, with a relaxing, holistic and healthy living approach to surfing through yoga. We strive to lure women away from their stressful, everyday lives and into the surf for one incredible, revitalising day!

#FITNESS: Strong it’s the new sexy!
Our Surf Fitness class will focus upon basic fitness concepts, body strength, flexibility and balance, all of which are applied during surfing. We encourage all levels of fitness to join in and encourage individuals to train at a pace they feel comfortable. The environment will be a very positive, supportive one; we are all on a journey of healthier living together.

#SURFING: Let the Ocean set you free!
Whether you are an experienced surfer or it’s your first time in the water, our instructors will cater to your specific needs, teaching you the basics of turning, paddling and getting up on your board, or improving your already existing skills.

Choose your level:

Beginner Surf Lesson (Level 1)
For those that are new to surfing, or never surfed before. Also for those that may have had a few surf lessons before but are still working on the basics, like your popup, Paddling, getting your weight forward on the board and riding. This includes:

- Beach awareness, safety, and session plan
- Know your board
- Ocean entry and board handling  
- The mount, positioning & paddling
- Whitewater gliding & manoeuvring
- The popup to surf stance methods
- Speed & manoeuvring

Progressive Improver Lesson (Level 2)
For those who are constantly popping up and riding broken whitewater and the occasional unbroken green wave. This includes:

- Beach awareness, safety, and session plan
- Beginner refresher, understanding your board and the waves
- Positioning & trimming
- Paddling for success
- The glide & popup   
- Compressions / extension for speed – the why, when, how
- Frontside & backside turns
- Bottom turns

#YOGA: Breath & Recover
Similar to the surfing, whether you're a veteran yogi or have never been to a class, our yoga teacher will be sure to tailor the class to all levels. It will encompass gentle movements, stretches and breathing techniques, all of which interrelate to the movements made whilst surfing. Presence, mindfulness and awareness, body alignment and connection, breathing and energy flow are all vital components of our everyday lives that will be explored throughout the class.

9.00am: Surf Class “surf like a woman!”

3.30pm: Debrief & finish

Our tour goes behind the scenes on a production tour of a winery. Closed toe shoes are a requirement of entry to the production area.

Included in your public wine tour will be transportation to and from your pick up location (choose from 2 locations in Sydney/multiple locations in the Hunter Valley), three wineries, lunch, the distillery, cheese and chocolate sampling.

**PLANNING YOUR DIVE BUSSELTON JETTY TOUR MEDICAL ISSUES** If you have existing medical issues that may preclude you from diving (asthma, epilepsy, heart condition, diabetes, vertigo, issues etc) you will need to get a Medical Form from your doctor to confirm you are fit and healthy to dive or do an undersea walk. Please bring this with you for your tour. Also attached is a copy of the Participant Record form you will be required to complete to do your dive. Feel free to have a look through it to understand the sort of questions that will be asked. (Please note that a positive response to any of the questions does not necessarily stop you from doing the tour - it just means our team need to talk through this issue with you to ensure it is safe for you to dive. If not, you will ALWAYS be given a 100% refund.)
 

START TIME AND WHERE TO MEET FOR YOUR TOUR The start time for your tour is when the tour begins at the Universal Access Platform. This is located at the DEEP END of the Jetty, 1.7 kilometers out to sea. So you will need to get to the Busselton Jetty AT LEAST 35-40 minutes before your tour's scheduled start time to find parking and make your way out to the end of the Jetty. Two options for getting to the end of the Jetty: a) walk out from the shore (will take 20-25 minutes, suggest you take water, sunscreen, hat and sunsmart clothing for the walk out.) b) book a train ticket out there online at the Busselton Jetty website www.busseltonjetty.com.au Please note that the Busselton Jetty train tickets will cost extra and you may need to walk back from the end of the Jetty at the end of your tour, depending if your tour finishes in time to catch the train back or if there are spare seats on the train. 

WHAT TO DO AND WHAT TO BRING Please: - arrive already wearing your bathers as there are no changing rooms available - go to the toilet before leaving shore, either at the Jetty Interpretative Centre or one of the other toilets along the foreshore as there are very limited toilet facilities at the end of the Jetty. - bring some water, a towel, sunsmart clothing to wear before and after your tour, sunglasses and hat, sunscreen and a credit card if there are great tour photos you want to purchase 

IF YOU ARE A DIVER - if you coming for a SCUBA dive on the Jetty, please bring your current dive certification card with you. NO CARD, NO DIVE unfortunately due to legal requirements associated with this. Additionally, to dive by yourself or on a dive tour or hire SCUBA gear for use on the Jetty you must have either a) dived in the last 12 months or b) done more than 30 logged dives and sign a form to confirm this.

**PLANNING YOUR DIVE BUSSELTON JETTY TOUR MEDICAL ISSUES** If you have existing medical issues that may preclude you from diving (asthma, epilepsy, heart condition, diabetes, vertigo, issues etc) you will need to get a Medical Form from your doctor to confirm you are fit and healthy to dive or do an undersea walk. Please bring this with you for your tour. Also attached is a copy of the Participant Record form you will be required to complete to do your dive. Feel free to have a look through it to understand the sort of questions that will be asked. (Please note that a positive response to any of the questions does not necessarily stop you from doing the tour - it just means our team need to talk through this issue with you to ensure it is safe for you to dive. If not, you will ALWAYS be given a 100% refund.)
 

START TIME AND WHERE TO MEET FOR YOUR TOUR The start time for your tour is when the tour begins at the Universal Access Platform. This is located at the DEEP END of the Jetty, 1.7 kilometers out to sea. So you will need to get to the Busselton Jetty AT LEAST 35-40 minutes before your tour's scheduled start time to find parking and make your way out to the end of the Jetty. Two options for getting to the end of the Jetty: a) walk out from the shore (will take 20-25 minutes, suggest you take water, sunscreen, hat and sunsmart clothing for the walk out.) b) book a train ticket out there online at the Busselton Jetty website www.busseltonjetty.com.au Please note that the Busselton Jetty train tickets will cost extra and you may need to walk back from the end of the Jetty at the end of your tour, depending if your tour finishes in time to catch the train back or if there are spare seats on the train. 

WHAT TO DO AND WHAT TO BRING Please: - arrive already wearing your bathers as there are no changing rooms available - go to the toilet before leaving shore, either at the Jetty Interpretative Centre or one of the other toilets along the foreshore as there are very limited toilet facilities at the end of the Jetty. - bring some water, a towel, sunsmart clothing to wear before and after your tour, sunglasses and hat, sunscreen and a credit card if there are great tour photos you want to purchase 

IF YOU ARE A DIVER - if you coming for a SCUBA dive on the Jetty, please bring your current dive certification card with you. NO CARD, NO DIVE unfortunately due to legal requirements associated with this. Additionally, to dive by yourself or on a dive tour or hire SCUBA gear for use on the Jetty you must have either a) dived in the last 12 months or b) done more than 30 logged dives and sign a form to confirm this.

Hi,

Thank you for booking a snorkel tour with us. We're really looking forward to taking you out and showing you why this coastline is such a special place to explore.

Depending on the conditions on the day, you might encounter some of our local favourites — cryptic nudibranchs, seahorses, and the lively kelp gardens that shelter Eden’s weedy sea dragons and curious wrasse.

It’s also common to see rays gliding along the sand, schools of fish, and the occasional octopus tucked into a rocky hideout. If we're lucky, we may even meet a friendly blue grouper or hear whales singing in the distance during migration season.

Below is some additional information to help you prepare for your tour, including forms to complete.

**Equipment**

All equipment can be pre‑booked for your use. If you already own personal items such as a mask or snorkel, you’re welcome to bring them along.

We also have equipment available for purchase if you’d like to start building your own dive kit.

**Approximate Schedule**

- 9:00 am — Meet at Strickland Lane, Eden, for paperwork and equipment collection
- 9:30 am — Self‑drive to snorkel site, or reserve one of three seats available with us
Sites are weather‑dependent and usually 5–25 minutes away
- 9:40 am — Equipment set‑up and snorkel briefing
- 10:00 am — Snorkel begins (approx. 45–90 minutes)
- Post‑snorkel — Debriefing and equipment care
- 12:00 pm — Approximate finish time

**What to Bring** 

- Snacks and water
- Personal items (sunscreen, etc.)
- Gear to get wet!
- Towel and warm clothes for after the snorkel
- Enthusiasm and a sense of adventure
- Completed forms attached here - [View Snorkel Dive SSI Forms.pdf](https://cdn.filestackcontent.com/UFPuE6bhSSSmWysk7WeJ) (or you’re welcome to fill them out on the day†)

**†Important Health Note**

Snorkelling is generally gentle and accessible, but it’s still important to be feeling well and comfortable in the water. 

The short questionnaire included in your forms helps ensure the experience is safe and enjoyable for you. Please answer the questions honestly. If anything is unclear, we can provide a more in‑depth **Diver Medical Participant Questionnaire** to help determine whether you should be assessed by a physician before participating, and we’re happy to chat through it before we head out.

**Location**

We’ll meet at the Dive Eden shed to collect equipment. You’ll find us on **Strickland Lane, Eden**, underneath **Brent Dunne Design**.

Alternatively, you can park on the main street and walk through the arcade between Mark Anthony’s and Anna Warren’s Gallery, then head down the staircase at the back.

Please note: Google Maps may direct you incorrectly. Look for BD Design, an open shed, and our green *Dive Eden* Landcruiser.

In the MySSI App, there is a section called **Courses** where you will find your materials - on the Website, the study materials are found under the **myTraining** Section.

If you have any questions, please let me know. We’re looking forward to snorkelling with you!

**Please note** that parking in Queenstown town centre is limited. You will need to allow additional time to find parking for your vehicle before boarding. We advise 30 minutes. There are parking lots available on Man Street and Church Street and free, limited parking down the Lake Esplanade.

##What to Bring
•        Non-slip shoes/ boots 
•        Waterproof jacket 
•        Warm sweater/fleece jacket
•        Sunscreen/sunglasses 
•        Insect repellent 
•        Swimwear (optional) 
•        Camera 
•        Overnight bag only
•        Personal medication, including for asthma and allergies
•        If booking includes an infant, guests are welcome to bring their own car seat if they wish

**Please note** that our quad share cabins are mixed gender, bunk-style compartments and you could potentially be sharing with other guests. If you would like to change to a private cabin, please reach out to our contact centre on 0800 65 65 01.

##Milford Sound Risk Disclosure

Visitors to Milford Sound should be aware of various natural hazards when going to Milford Sound. 

**Aotearoa New Zealand**
- Powerful natural forces have shaped Aotearoa New Zealand over millions of years. Earthquakes and volcanoes lifted these beautiful islands out of the Pacific Ocean. They have created the dramatic landscapes we enjoy today.
- Natural hazards are part of life here. Around 20,000 earthquakes are recorded each year. Most are small and go unnoticed, but larger events can cause damage. Understanding the hazards and how to stay safe is an important part of planning your visit. 

**Piopiotahi Milford Sound**
- Dramatic and ever-changing, Piopiotahi Milford Sound is one of the world’s most spectacular and special environments. Its steep, glacier-carved mountains and deep fiord have been shaped by powerful geological forces over millions of years.
- The area is exposed to risk from a range of natural hazards. These can occur at any time, and some can happen without warning. Of all the hazards, large earthquakes, landslides and tsunamis pose the greatest risk to people at Piopiotahi Milford Sound.
- It is extremely unlikely that one will happen during your visit, especially for a short stay. However, there is a risk and the longer you spend there, the higher it becomes. Once you are there, your safety options are limited and it is important you understand the risks, before you go.

**Earthquakes at Piopiotahi Milford Sound**
- Like the rest of Aotearoa New Zealand, small earthquakes occur regularly in Fiordland. We don’t feel them and they don’t bother us. These small movements are a normal part of how the land works and do not pose a risk to people.
Sometimes, earthquakes in or near Fiordland are felt at Piopiotahi Milford Sound. They might shake objects on a shelf or rattle a window, but they do not cause major impacts or disrupt your visit.
- Occasionally, a stronger earthquake can trigger avalanches, rockfall or landslides. These can cause debris to fall onto roads, jetties and tracks, and may disrupt your travel plans if you happen to be nearby.
- Large earthquakes are rare, and extremely unlikely to happen during a short visit. But they will happen again.
- The Alpine Fault runs almost the entire length of the South Island and crosses the entrance to Piopiotahi Milford Sound. It can generate earthquakes of magnitude 8 or greater, occurring on average every 300 years. There is a 75% chance of this happening in the next 50 years (find out more at [af8.org.nz)](https://af8.org.nz/). An earthquake of this size would almost certainly affect the narrow waterway and surrounding area.

**What to do in an earthquake:**
- DROP, COVER and HOLD until shaking stops. Most injuries from earthquakes happen when you try and move during the shaking. The lower to the ground/floor you are, the less likely you are to be injured.
- Follow staff instructions and/or move up and away from waterways (the fiord and rivers) as quickly as possible.

For more detailed information, please visit [Emergency Management Southland](https://civildefencesouthland.govt.nz/piopiotahi-milford-sound) or [AF8](https://af8.org.nz/).

There is a 75% chance of this happening in the next 50 years (find out more at [af8.org.nz)](https://af8.org.nz/). An earthquake of this size would almost certainly affect the narrow waterway and surrounding area.

**What to do in an earthquake:**
- DROP, COVER and HOLD until shaking stops. Most injuries from earthquakes happen when you try and move during the shaking. The lower to the ground/floor you are, the less likely you are to be injured.
- Follow staff instructions and/or move up and away from waterways (the fiord and rivers) as quickly as possible.

For more detailed information, please visit [Emergency Management Southland](https://civildefencesouthland.govt.nz/piopiotahi-milford-sound) or [AF8](https://af8.org.nz/).

.**

Thanks for choosing your adventure with WAM! We can't wait for you to join us on a spectacular journey into nature.

Just by booking with us, you have done a lot of good for the planet, congratulations! (read on for more details of how)

Before we do so, please take a minute to read some important information about your tour:

- WAM Adventures require a minimum of 4 people to run. We almost always run our trips but we'll be in contact as we get closer to the date for updates.
- You’ll start receiving emails as we get closer to the date.
- Once you have a date confirmed, if you need to cancel, we require a minimum 7 days notice to provide a refund (please read our T&C's for other options) 

##Pick up Location
We meet at The Peninsula Hot Springs on the Mornington Peninsula. Please contact us if you would like to discuss an alternative pick up location on the Mornington Peninsula. 

##Gift vouchers
If you have a gift voucher, you'll need to redeem it at some stage by returning to the relevant tour page, selecting a date and entering the voucher code at the checkout - think of your voucher as like a pre-paid credit card
Also, we can’t extend the use-by date on gift vouchers past three years (three years is pretty good!)

##Premium Service
- We include everything you need on your adventure including activities, equipment, food and refreshments. 

- To maximise your comfort we even provide you with eco-pack for the day which includes some special gifts and products from local businesses that directly support the environment. This includes free sunscreen and a towel service. You simply hand these back at the end of your experience. Its a bit like a pack you may get on a first class flight or a luxury hotel, except ours is good for the planet!

##Now for the deep and meaningful:
By booking an adventure with us you have directly helped make a long-term positive environmental and social impact by:
- Planting native trees on the Mornington Peninsula with MP Koalas to capture carbon emissions, protect our climate, enhance soil and water quality, and restore habitat for native wildlife. 
- Regenerate reefs and native kelp locally with The Nature Conservancy, providing marine habitat, filtering seawater, removing nitrogen and phosphate, and preventing used shell from entering landfill.
- Support female education with The Stars Foundation which empowers and supports Indigenous young women and girls to complete education and find work.
- Protect and plant mangroves to protect our coastlines, wildlife and support blue carbon projects.

You'll find additional information relevant to your adventure on the Wild Adventures Melbourne website. Please check the website for exactly what items we recommend bringing with you on the day.

##Green is our Gold Commitment:

As members of Australia’s tourism industry, we believe a land as precious
as ours should be preserved for generations to come. As a visitor, we ask that you do the same. That’s why we’ve set some unwritten rules that have kept our backyard beautiful for thousands of years.

Passed down through story and practice, they’re how we walk gently, listen deeply, tread with care – and look out for each other along the way. 

By following them throughout your visit, you too can care for Australia when you Come and say G’day.

Consider these principles a bit of local knowledge. A few fundamentals to help you respect this place and have an unforgettable stay in the process.

The Guiding Principles:

Celebrate Community
The best part of an Australian visit is the people you meet.
Shop local, engage with communities, and you’ll leave with new mates aplenty.

Embrace Culture
Australia’s cultural diversity stretches from ancient songlines to city laneways. Immerse yourself in it all - honour First Nations cultures, embrace our diversity, and you’ll leave with new knowledge and new friends.

Preserve Place
In Australia you’ll find some of the most unspoilt landscapes on Earth. Help keep them that way by minimising your impact wherever you go.

Respect Wildlife
Australia has some of the most unique animals on the planet. Take as many photos as you like but remember to give them space and respect their homes.

Take Care
We look out for one another in Australia, but it’s important to take care of yourself too. Listen to the land, respect it, and always put safety first.


If you have any questions between now and your trip with us, please don't hesitate to email or call me directly.

Looking forward to adventuring with you soon,

Nic 'Coops' Cooper
WAM Founder

Have you ever wanted to snorkel with manta rays and experience the breathtaking Ningaloo Reef?
This full day tour takes you around to the most spectacular locations! We take both divers and snorkelers together on board this day tour!
Experience the unique opportunity to snorkel up close with our resident population of these amazing creatures, Manta Rays, and SCUBA dive or snorkel the world heritage listed Ningaloo Reef!!
The full day tour meets at 8:00am and returns between 14:30 and 15:30. We start by checking you in at our shop (Shop 8, Coral Bay Arcade) where we will provide you with all the equipment you need for the day. Then, we head down to the jetty on our buses to begin the days adventure!
This tour includes 2 dives or 2 snorkels on the incredible Ningaloo reef. Here, you will have the opportunity to see a variety of tropical fish, possibly turtles, sharks and definitely beautiful coral structures. In between the 2 dives/snorkels we head out into Batemans Bay, a sandy bottom bay and send our spotter plane out in search for manta rays. If we are successful in locating manta rays, you will then you will have the opportunity to snorkel with them.
Once we have completed our manta ray interaction portion of the day we will cruise around the bay in search of other marine animals while the crew prepare lunch. We provide a buffet style lunch on board and can accommodate for any dietary requirements. Once we have filled our bellies, we head back over to the Ningaloo reef and enter the water for our final in water activity! We then head back to the jetty and finish the day back at the shop.
Information for Divers
Our dive sites are beautiful coral reef dives that have a varied depth of 4m to 12m with our average depth being at 6-8m. As the Ningaloo Reef is a fringing reef, it is quite shallow all around but filled with spectacular coral structures and marine life. All of our dives are guided dives with maximum group sizes of 8, although we typically have smaller groups.
Our dives are 45-50 minutes long and the average visibility in Coral Bay is 10-15m but can vary depending on conditions. The water temperature varies from 20C up to 26C in the summer and we provide full length 5mm wetsuits for all divers.

meta_raw_booking_notes:
We can't wait for you to go on a spectacular journey into nature.

Just by booking with us, you have done a lot of good for the planet, congratulations! (read on for more details of how)

Before we do so, please take a minute to read some important information about your tour:
- If you need to cancel, we require a minimum 7 days notice to provide a refund (please read our T&C's for other options)
Please check in and sign the waiver prior to the date of your adventure.
We also provide you with an insulated picnic backpack, with picnic mat and everything else you need for the perfect day out. Please return this along with any equipment at the end of your adventure.

##Meet Location
Torello Farm, 410 White Hill Rd, Dromana VIC 3936
This is where you collect your picnic pack and coordinates from to your secret adventure picnic location. Head to the counter to collect.

##Gift vouchers
If you have a gift voucher, you'll need to redeem it at some stage by returning to the relevant tour page, selecting a date and entering the voucher code at the checkout - think of your voucher as like a pre-paid credit card
Also, we can’t extend the use-by date on gift vouchers past three years (three years is pretty good!)

##Now for the deep and meaningful:
By booking an adventure with us you have directly helped make a long-term positive environmental and social impact by:
- Planting native trees on the Mornington Peninsula with MP Koalas to capture carbon emissions, protect our climate, enhance soil and water quality, and restore habitat for native wildlife. 
- Regenerate reefs and native kelp locally with The Nature Conservancy, providing marine habitat, filtering seawater, removing nitrogen and phosphate, and preventing used shell from entering landfill.
- Support female education with The Stars Foundation which empowers and supports Indigenous young women and girls to complete education and find work.
- Protect and plant mangroves to protect our coastlines, wildlife and support blue carbon projects.

You'll find additional information relevant to your adventure on the Wild Adventures Melbourne website. Please check the website for exactly what items we recommend bringing with you on the day.

##Green is our Gold Commitment:

As members of Australia’s tourism industry, we believe a land as precious
as ours should be preserved for generations to come. As a visitor, we ask that you do the same. That’s why we’ve set some unwritten rules that have kept our backyard beautiful for thousands of years.

Passed down through story and practice, they’re how we walk gently, listen deeply, tread with care – and look out for each other along the way. 

By following them throughout your visit, you too can care for Australia when you Come and say G’day.

Consider these principles a bit of local knowledge. A few fundamentals to help you respect this place and have an unforgettable stay in the process.

The Guiding Principles:

Celebrate Community
The best part of an Australian visit is the people you meet.
Shop local, engage with communities, and you’ll leave with new mates aplenty.

Embrace Culture
Australia’s cultural diversity stretches from ancient songlines to city laneways. Immerse yourself in it all - honour First Nations cultures, embrace our diversity, and you’ll leave with new knowledge and new friends.

Preserve Place
In Australia you’ll find some of the most unspoilt landscapes on Earth. Help keep them that way by minimising your impact wherever you go.

Respect Wildlife
Australia has some of the most unique animals on the planet. Take as many photos as you like but remember to give them space and respect their homes.

Take Care
We look out for one another in Australia, but it’s important to take care of yourself too. Listen to the land, respect it, and always put safety first.


If you have any questions between now and your trip with us, please don't hesitate to email or call me directly.

Have a great adventure.

Nic 'Coops' Cooper
WAM Founder

Download The App / Free Surf Lesson Notifications!
Our classes run every day surf is up and by downloading the Wellington Surf Lessons App you can receive notifications on your phone 2-3 days prior to when we are running classes. This is important as lessons are surf/weather dependant which means we may not have all our lesson times available on the calendar until a few days prior.
Note: If you have booked a surf lesson in advance and the weather conditions are not suitable for surfing we will offer you an alternative day to book.
Cost
$89 / surfer (Includes all equipment!)
For discounts on multiple surf lessons - please see Surf Lesson Packages (For individual surfers only)
Duration
2 Hours
About
Wellington Surf Lesson offer super fun group classes for both beginner through to intermediate level students and cater for students of all ages, from kids as young as 7 years old surfing with their parents through to adults of all ages.
Lessons are progressive so we recommend students take 2-3 beginner lessons alongside some practise rentals then 2-3 intermediate classes.
You can buy singular lessons, or for an even better deal, you can buy a Package Deals! and receive multiple lessons at a discount rate (For individual surfers only).
Once you've got your surfing to where it needs to be, you can book a FREE Consultation with one of our instructors on the best equipment to buy based on your current surfing ability and goals.
Classes To Choose From
Beginners Classes (Option 1)
Beginner classes will focus on all the important fundamentals you should know before hitting the water by yourself E.g. beach safety, body positioning, basic pop up techniques, catching waves in the white water and more. After taking a few classes we highly recommend students do some practise rentals to practise by them selves.
Intermediate Classes (Option 2)
Intermediate classes will focus on riding unbroken waves, how to get through the waves properly, correct positioning to catch unbroken waves, how to turn and ride across the wave, advance pop up techniques and much more! These classes are suitable for students who have taken at least 2-3 beginner classes, had some practise by them selves and are feeling confident with their pop up in white water.
Recommended Lesson Plan
The lessons are progressive so we recommend students take the following lesson plan:
x3 beginner lessons alongside some practise rentals
x3 intermediate classes alongside some practise rentals
Private lessons with our expert instructors to fine tune your surfing further
Whats Included
We use the Surfing NZ Approved Softboards which are easy to balance, paddle, stand & turn on
Super warm C-Skins wetsuits
2 hours of expert instruction from qualified Surfing NZ Instructors
Discounts on boards, wetsuits and accessories at our surf shop called Wellington Surf Co based in Miramar

If you need some individual help during our group classes, don't hesitate to chat with just one of the team at the start of the lesson about your current surfing experience and what you feel you need help with. We will then give you some individual help during the class to fine tune your surfing.
About Kids
The group lessons are a mixed class of adults and kids so you can surf with your kids! Or if you prefer, a private group lesson or birthday party can be arranged just for the kids. All kids are provided with the right surfboard and wetsuit to get them having the most fun and learning quicker.

Chat with a supportive group of like minded surfers who are also learning to surf

- Rest well the night before and ensure you're well hydrated prior to the trip

All participants must follow the guidelines and instructions provided by crew at all times.

For your safety, remain seated while the vessel is in motion.  

**Moving Around the Boat**
1. Use both hands to hold railings or stable surfaces  
2. Be mindful of trip hazards and slippery surfaces  
3. Avoid moving around if the sea is rough or the weather is windy  
4. Exercise extra caution when using stairs; keep your hands free to hold handrails  

**Child Supervision**
Children must be supervised by a responsible adult at all times

Explore remote and rarely visited wilderness
Rates
Total $4250 ($400 Deposit priced per person)
Duration
8 Days
About
Amazing wilderness days with challenges, rewards and remote, dramatic landscapes.
Fly across World Heritage coastlines and mountain ranges to land deep in Southwest Tasmania – explore the wilderness waterways of Bathurst Harbour and Port Davey by sea kayak – paddle through changing landscapes from campsite to campsite – these are the attractions and challenges of our 8-Day Sea Kayaking Expedition.
Bathurst Harbour and Port Davey, in Tasmania’s Wilderness World Heritage Area, offer a combination of sheltered wilderness harbours, rugged ocean coastlines, remote islands and wild rivers. There are no roads and no settlements. Discover spectacular destinations in the best way possible – by water, at paddling pace.
Our guides know this pristine wilderness intimately – all the sheltered bays and open beaches, the peaks and islands, every hidden corner and comfortable campsite. After a spectacular flight to the remote airstrip at Melaleuca, your days will be spent exploring one of Tasmania’s most remote and beautiful coastlines, paddling through perfect reflections in the tannin-stained waters, beneath mountains that rise from the shore and calling in to sandy beaches.
This trip has a flexible itinerary with time for optional short walks or relaxing on the beach. Your nights will be spent in remote and hidden campsites. Every night you'll enjoy delicious food with a glass of wine.
Extensive kayaking experience is not necessary, but it is important to have a sound level of fitness, be comfortable with wilderness camping and, most of all, have a sense of adventure.
About the Tour
The adventure begins...
The journey begins at Cambridge Airport near Hobart with a 40-50 minute scenic flight. Our pilot decides whether to fly along the remote beaches of the South Coast, or over the wild Eastern Arthur Ranges before landing on the gravel strip at Melaleuca.
Our first night is spent here, giving us all time to immerse ourselves in the relaxed pace of the Southwest Tasmanian wilderness. After setting up camp we will provide an orientation of the sea kayaks. There will also be time to explore Melaleuca, including the Deny King Museum, Needwonee Aboriginal Interpretative Walk, historic tin mining areas and looking out for the endangered Orange-bellied Parrots who breed here over summer.
The first evening your guides will, over a convivial glass of wine, discuss itinerary options for the expedition after careful assessment of the weather conditions. We’re kayaking in a remote wilderness area and there are plenty of options for outstanding paddling destinations.
An example itinerary is available for download from our website!
The trip package for 8 days includes:
Transfers between Hobart and Cambridge Airport
Scenic 40-50 minute return flight from Hobart to Melaleuca
All meals (with an emphasis on fresh Tasmanian produce) and refreshments, a glass of wine each evening
Good quality camping equipment specifically selected for wilderness safety and comfort
Two highly-experienced kayaking guides
Comfortable and stable double sea kayaks
All specialist paddling equipment (good-quality paddle, paddling jacket, spray deck, buoyancy vest, duffle bag, and dry-bags)
National park entry fees

meta_raw_description:
Have you ever wanted to explore the amazing Ningaloo Reef?
This full day experience will take you on a adventure exploring the spectacular diving and snorkelling locations on the world heritage listed Ningaloo Reef.
You will have the unique opportunity to snorkel with manta rays, observe humpback whales as they migrate along our coast and SCUBA dive or snorkel at one of our favourite locations.
The tour meets at 8am and returns around 3pm. We start the day by checking you in at our shop (Shop 8, Coral Bay Arcade) where we will provide you with your equipment that you need for the day. From there we will travel to the jetty on our buses to begin the tour.
This tour includes a snorkel or dive on the incredible Ningaloo Reef where you have the chance to see a variety of tropical fish, possibly turtles, sharks and beautiful coral structures.
From here, we will head into the next bay area and send out spotter plane in search for manta rays. If we are successful in our search, then you would have the opportunity to snorkel with them.
Next we will cruise the bay in search of other marine animals while the crew prepare lunch. Following lunch, we will head outside the reef in search of humpback whales to view as they migrate and frolic their way along our coastline. Then it's time to head back to the jetty and finish the day back at the shop.
Information for SCUBA Divers
Our dive sites are beautiful coral reefs that have a varied depth of 4m to 12m, with the average depth being at 6-9m. As Ningaloo Reef is a fringing reef system, it is quite shallow all around but filled with spectacular coral structures and marine life. All of our dives are guided with a maximum group size of 8, although typically we have smaller groups.
Our dives are 45-50 minutes long and average visibility in Coral Bay is 10-15m but can vary depending on conditions. The water temperature varies from 20C up to 26C in the summer months and we provide full length 5mm wetsuits for our divers.

When you go on an overseas or on an interstate holiday you put a lot of time and effort, not to mention the money to ensure everything is just perfect for you and your family. Well Brighton Coach and Tours has the perfect day for you. In fact, we have named our Port Stephens Day Tour “One Perfect Day”. Yes, you are going to leave the metropolitan magic of Sydney to venture or should I say adventure to the pristine waters of Port Stephens and the spectacular sand dunes of Stockton Bight. Just a 2.5 hours’ drive north in a luxury state the art modern coach to a marine wonderland of dolphins all year round and whales in the winter. Departing Sydney’s iconic Central Railway Station at 7am you will be guided past some of Sydney’s best landmarks. Our local guides will provide informative facts about Hyde Park, NSW Parliament House and the Origins of old Sydney town, Australia’s first convict settlement. As you depart the Sydney CBD you will be stunned by views of the Sydney Harbour Bridge, the Sydney Opera House and the world’s most beautiful harbour, the one and only Sydney Harbour. Now it’s time to sit back and relax as we travel north along the M1 highway into the rugged Hawkesbury River region, a true bushland wilderness and one of Australia’s great rivers only 1 hour from the Sydney CDB. Leaving the mighty Hawkesbury region we stop briefly at what
the locals refer to as ‘The Twin Servo’s’ for coffee and a comfort stop. As we leave the M1 we are now in the Port Stephens local government area and the lands of
the traditional indigenous Worimi people. Next, we arrive at the Stockton Bight sand dunes, a coastal desert 32kms long and largest mobile sand dune system in the Southern Hemisphere. Stockton Bight will take your breath away. Here you will be warmly greeted by our friendly 4WD drivers and guides from Port Stephens 4WD Tours, who will help you onto their 19 seater 4WD red coaches for the 2km drive to “The Dunes”. It can be a little bit bumpy on the track to the Dunes as we navigate the ‘Woopdie Doos’, a series corrugated sand berms. Ok, now it’s time for Sandboarding. Your sandboarding guide will give you safety instructions and tips on techniques on how to sandboard successfully. Sandboarding is suitable for toddlers to grandparents and very safe. Sandboarding is referred to as ‘soft adventure’ however it is hard core family fun. So now it’s time to shake off that sand to go the tranquil coastal village of Nelson Bay, the heart of Port Stephens and home to Delbora Marina departure point for the your Dolphin Discovery Cruise. Before your cruise there is plenty of time to enjoy your lunch at the many waterside cafes or simply walk around sightseeing and taking in the seaside vibe.
Ok now it’s time to board your boat to see a marine wonderland with Moonshadow TQC Cruises, the largest dolphin cruise company in NSW. Port Stephens is home to 160 bottle nose dolphins, one of the most beautiful marine mammals on the planet. At times the dolphins love to surf the bow waves of Moonshadow’s boats and if you’re lucky they may give you a wink of their eye or you can just wink at them. There is heaps of other wildlife to see on the cruise from pelicans, sea eagles and even the odd seal. You will experience 90 minutes of cruising the blue blue waters of Port Stephens with expert commentary provided by Moonshadow’s experienced skippers. In the warmer months you can even take a plunge in the boom net at the rear of the boat but make sure you have a change of clothes. Take plenty of photos to capture these magic moments. You tired yet? It’s now time head south back to Sydney. But before we leave Port Stephens there is one last stop at B-Farm aka Murrays Brewery for a spot of wine tasting. B Farm has several exquisite wines for you to sample. They also have a stunning gift shop for you to buy the perfect gift for that special someone back home. All Aboard! Time to head back to the big smoke. So put your seat belt, press recline on your seat because it’s time for some shut eye on our trip back Sydney. So as the bus pulls back into Central Railway I’m sure you will say “that was One Perfect Day”. See you on the next our tour to the Blue Mountains if you haven’t already been. Now that’s a whole another story.

Check in: 9:30am

Every guest MUST complete the online waiver before check-in. We’d appreciate it if you could complete this in advance to help avoid any delays on the day.

###Check-in: 
Please make your own way to Coral Sea Marina. The vessel will depart on time. Please be at departure point 30 minutes prior to departure for check in. 
It is advisable to bring a rain jacket during the summer months (Jan - April) and warmer clothes during the winter months (approx June - October). 
##Bring your own alcohol and soft drinks. (just nothing in a glass bottle or red wine)

###Waiver & Snorkeling Assessment Requirements
- All tours require participants to complete an online waiver at least 24 hours prior to departure.
- If the online waiver is not completed within this timeframe, you will be required to fill out a paper waiver at the marina during check-in.
- Please arrive at the marina 30 minutes before departure to allow sufficient time for check-in and paperwork, avoiding any delays.

###Snorkeling Tours
- For all snorkeling tours, participants must complete a snorkeling assessment form, which will be issued on the day. This form helps our crew assess your swimming ability, communication needs, and any required assistance while in the water to ensure your safety.
- If you do not meet the necessary requirements in the snorkeling assessment, the skipper reserves the right to request that you remain onboard for your safety.

• Free use of snorkeling equipment - mask/snorkel provided (excluding prescription masks) **To reduce damage to coral, we do not provide fins**
• Lunch and snacks
• Environmental Marine Charge 
• Queensland Parks and Wildlife Charge
• Fuel levy

###What to bring:
• Sunscreen, sunglasses, a towel and a hat
• Practical clothing and footwear (warmer items during winter)
• Underwater camera
• BYO alcohol and soft drinks/soda (no glass or red wine) for the boat only

Important - Please read this first!
Here you can book in lessons for you and your friends on the available calendar dates.

For discounts on multiple surf lessons and a progressive lesson approach, please see our Package Deals!
Important:
New lesson times will be added to the calendar each week so please check the booking calendar regularly for available times slots.
Download The App / Free Surf Lesson Notifications!
Our classes run every day surf is up and by downloading the Wellington Surf Lessons App you can receive notifications on your phone 2-3 days prior to when we are running classes. This is important as lessons are surf/weather dependant which means we may not have all our lesson times available on the calendar until a few days prior.
Note: If you have booked a surf lesson in advance and the weather conditions are not suitable for surfing we will offer you an alternative day to book.
Rates
$89 / surfer (Includes all equipment!)
For discounts on multiple surf lessons - please see Surf Lesson Packages (For individual surfers only)
Duration
2 Hours
About
Wellington Surf Lesson offer super fun group classes for both beginner through to intermediate level students and cater for students of all ages, from kids as young as 7 years old surfing with their parents through to adults of all ages.
Lessons are progressive so we recommend students take 2-3 beginner lessons alongside some practise rentals then 2-3 intermediate classes.
See Package Deals!
Once you've got your surfing to where it needs to be, you can book a FREE Consultation with one of our instructors on the best equipment to buy based on your current surfing ability and goals.
Classes To Choose From
Beginners Classes (Option 1)
Beginner classes will focus on all the important fundamentals you should know before hitting the water by yourself E.g. beach safety, body positioning, basic pop up techniques, catching waves in the white water and more. After taking a few classes we highly recommend students do some practise rentals to practise by them selves.
Intermediate Classes (Option 2)
Intermediate classes will focus on riding unbroken waves, how to get through the waves properly, correct positioning to catch unbroken waves, how to turn and ride across the wave, advance pop up techniques and much more! These classes are suitable for students who have taken at least 2-3 beginner classes, had some practise by them selves and are feeling confident with their pop up in white water.
Recommended Lesson Plan
The lessons are progressive so we recommend students take the following lesson plan:
x3 beginner lessons alongside some practise rentals
x3 intermediate classes alongside some practise rentals
Private lessons with our expert instructors to fine tune your surfing further
For discounts on multiple surf lessons and a progressive lesson approach, please see our Package Deals!

We use the Surfing NZ Approved Softboards which are easy to balance, paddle, stand & turn on
Super warm C-Skins wetsuits
2 hours of expert instruction from qualified Surfing NZ Instructors
Discounts on boards, wetsuits and accessories at our surf shop called Wellington Surf Co based in Miramar
Extra Accessories
Booties, gloves and hoods are $10 a pair and need to be booked and paid for on arrival. Will be first in first served on available sizes.
Need some individual help during the classes?
If you need some individual help during our group classes, don't hesitate to chat with just one of the team at the start of the lesson about your current surfing experience and what you feel you need help with. We will then give you some individual help during the class to fine tune your surfing.
About Kids
The group lessons are a mixed class of adults and kids so you can surf with your kids! Or if you prefer, a private group lesson or birthday party can be arranged just for the kids. All kids are provided with the right surfboard and wetsuit to get them having the most fun and learning quicker.
Important: For less experienced kids or kids younger than 11 we require the parent to supervise them at knee height in the water at all times during the class.
What To Bring
Swim wear
Towel
Drinking water
Sunscreen
Download The App
Download the Wellington Surf Lessons App and you'll receive:
Notifications on your phone 2-3 days prior to when the surf is best and we are running surf classes & rentals.
Chat with a supportive group of like minded surfers who are also learning to surf
Get your questions answered by the community and our instructor team
Buy and or sell surf equipment
Download the Wellington Surf Lessons App for FREE!
Surf Shop
Loving your surfing and keen to buy your own surf equipment this summer??? Well come check out our surf shop in Miramar!
We are offer our students discounts on all our surf school approved equipment.
Come in and talk to our friendly team. We are here to fit you with the right equipment and give you all the guidance and support you need.
Simply text us on 0211764073 to make a time to meet us at the shop.
Wellington Surf Shop
Location
We are a mobile surf school and our trailer is located at the beach carpark at the end of the South Beach Access Road by Arnold Park. Please meet 30min before your lesson at the trailer for check-in.
South Beach Access Road, Tītahi Bay, Porirua 5022
Note: We also sell equipment and have a surf training area at our Surf School Surf Shop in Miramar called Wellington Surf Co.
