#Welcome aboard your Fantasea Cruising / My Fast Ferry 9pm or Midnight Fireworks Cruise on New Year’s Eve

New Year’s Eve is fast approaching, and we hope you are as excited as we are about being on beautiful Sydney Harbour to experience the world’s most iconic fireworks display. 

With all the hustle and bustle that New Year’s Eve offers, please find some valuable information below to help make your boarding process easier.

##Your Vessel

Your cruise is on our vessel **SeaCat 1**. Please take the time to look at the image of your vessel below as Darling Harbour is a very busy area on New Year’s Eve and there will be many vessels departing on the night.

![SeaCat 1](https://www.fantasea.com.au/wp-content/uploads/sites/1538/2025/12/seacat1.jpg)

##Departure Times

- The departure time of your **9pm Fireworks Cruise** is **19:45** sharp from **Darling Harbour – Pier 26, Berth 2**. 
- The departure time of your **Midnight Fireworks Cruise** is **22:30** sharp from **Darling Harbour – King Street Wharf 9**. 

## Check In

- Please check in at least **120 minutes prior to your scheduled departure time** 
- Please bring a **printed or digital copy of your booking confirmation** and check in with one of our team
- At check in you will receive a **boarding wristband** for your cruise.
- **Check in is available at the Fantasea Cruising Office from 12:00 on Wednesday the 31st of December.**

##Check in location is the Fantasea Cruising Darling Harbour Office at Pier 26 (Directly underneath Helm Bar)

![Darling Harbour](https://www.fantasea.com.au/wp-content/uploads/sites/1538/2025/12/dh_office_map.jpg)
 
## Fraud Prevention

Please present the credit card that was used to pay for your booking and matching valid photo identification. The name listed on your credit card should match the name listed on your booking.

##Boarding

Please make your way to your departure wharf at least 45 minutes before your scheduled departure time. Fantasea Cruising staff will be on location to manage the queue and may allow less mobile passengers to move to the front.


##What to Bring

- You are welcome to bring along snacks and meals. Some snacks will be available for purchase onboard.
- **No BYO alcohol allowed**. There is a licensed bar on board for alcoholic beverages and soft drinks
- Appropriate clothing for the weather conditions on the night
- Please bring a **printed or digital copy of your booking confirmation** as you may need to show this to security personnel at various access points around Darling Harbour.

##On the Night

More than a million people will be making their way into the city for the celebrations. Please find details on road closures and public transport on New Year’s Eve below to help you plan your night.

- [**Public Transport**](https://www.sydneynewyearseve.com/transport)
- [**Road Closures**](https://www.sydneynewyearseve.com/road-closures/)

We very much look forward to having you on board with us to enjoy what promises to be one of the most spectacular events of the year!

Kind Regards,

The Fantasea Cruising / My Fast Ferry team

meta_raw_booking_notes:
#Welcome aboard your Fantasea Cruising / My Fast Ferry 9pm or Midnight Fireworks Cruise on New Year’s Eve

New Year’s Eve is fast approaching, and we hope you are as excited as we are about being on beautiful Sydney Harbour to experience the world’s most iconic fireworks display. 

With all the hustle and bustle that New Year’s Eve offers, please find some valuable information below to help make your boarding process easier.

##Your Vessel

Your cruise is on our vessel **Ocean Tracker**. Please take the time to look at the image of your vessel below as Darling Harbour is a very busy area on New Year’s Eve and there will be many vessels departing on the night.

![Ocean Tracker](https://assets.myfastferry.com.au/images/2022/12/28123935/nye_ocean_tracker.jpg)

##Departure Times

- The departure time of your **9pm Fireworks Cruise** is **19:45** sharp from **Darling Harbour – Pier 26, Berth 7**. 
- The departure time of your **Midnight Fireworks Cruise** is **22:15** sharp from **Darling Harbour – Pier 26, Berth 4**. 

## Check In

- Please check in at least **120 minutes prior to your scheduled departure time** 
- Please bring a **printed or digital copy of your booking confirmation** and check in with one of our team
- At check in you will receive a **boarding wristband** for your cruise.
- **Check in is available at the Fantasea Cruising Office from 12:00 on Wednesday, 31st December.**

##Check in location is the Fantasea Cruising Darling Harbour Office at Pier 26 (Directly underneath Helm Bar)

![Darling Harbour](https://www.fantasea.com.au/wp-content/uploads/sites/1538/2025/12/dh_office_map.jpg)
 
## Fraud Prevention

Please present the credit card that was used to pay for your booking and matching valid photo identification. The name listed on your credit card should match the name listed on your booking.

##Boarding

Please make your way to your departure wharf at least 45 minutes before your scheduled departure time. Fantasea Cruising staff will be on location to manage the queue and may allow less mobile passengers to move to the front.


##What to Bring

- You are welcome to bring along snacks and meals. Some snacks will be available for purchase onboard.
- **No BYO alcohol allowed**. There is a licensed bar on board for alcoholic beverages and soft drinks
- Appropriate clothing for the weather conditions on the night
- Please bring a **printed or digital copy of your booking confirmation** as you may need to show this to security personnel at various access points around Darling Harbour.

##On the Night

More than a million people will be making their way into the city for the celebrations. Please find details on road closures and public transport on New Year’s Eve below to help you plan your night.

- [**Public Transport**](https://www.sydneynewyearseve.com/transport)
- [**Road Closures**](https://www.sydneynewyearseve.com/road-closures/)

We very much look forward to having you on board with us to enjoy what promises to be one of the most spectacular events of the year!

Kind Regards,

The Fantasea Cruising / My Fast Ferry team

meta_raw_description: Join the working crew aboard the 45ft catamaran Queimarla for an expedition-style 3 or 5 day course along Western Australia’s stunning coast. You’ll stand watches, steer, set sails, study weather, night-sail and take part in onboard living tasks while exploring remote islands, snorkelling, fishing and swimming. The course focuses on practical seamanship and safety, and successful participants earn internationally recognised IYT certificates to help them charter yachts worldwide. The atmosphere balances intensive training with time for adventure and camaraderie.
meta_raw_booking_notes:
#Thank you for booking your sailing adventure with us... we are looking forward to sailing with you and helping you achieve your sailing dreams!
 
There are a few things to do prior to joining. 
Please read the following information carefully (including any relevant links) below to make sure you are fully prepared for your adventure.

This course has been designed around an expedition along the Western Australian Coast where you will be part of a working crew, participating in all the skills you need to become a competent yachts person.
You will be trained to take over command of the yacht and by the end of the course should be able to handle the vessel safely and competently.
You will be studying an IYT sailing course and graduate with an internationally recognized certificate that will allow you to charter yachts around the world.
We will also fit in plenty of adventure including swimming, snorkelling, fishing, exploring and friendship.

Check our website to learn more about our sailing catamaran [Queimarla](https://www.adventuresailing.com.au/catamaran-queimarla). She is a 45ft high performance sailing machine which is fully certified by AMSA (Australian Maritime Safety Authority) 
Your captain/instructor [Captain Paul](https://www.adventuresailing.com.au/the-team) is a fully qualified professional skipper (Master 45m) with over 35 years sailing experience. Few people know the coast as well as him. You can rest assured that you will be in safe hands on a very sea worthy vessel! 


##There are 3 courses that can be completed during a 5-day course. The one you study will depend on your experience and your training needs. 

***Option 1. International Crew Certificates (3 day summer trips)***
•	This course has NO prerequisites. 
•	Minimum age 16. 
•	This course is often chosen if folks require less training, therefore allowing more time for relaxing and enjoying the environment. (Less work more play) 
•	This is a good introductory level, covering all the skills required to sail a large catamaran safely & competently. 
•    More information on this course [HERE](https://www.iytworld.com/courses/international-crew-training/)

***Option 2. International Flotilla Skipper (5 day winter trips)*** 
•.      You must hold a Marine Radio licence before the issue of this certificate. (This can be done on board during your course.) 
•	Minimum age 16 years old. 
•	This is a high-level training course with the aim of skilling you to be able to take command of a vessel up to 24m. 
•	This certificate will allow you to charter yachts. 
•      This qualification can be converted to an ICC cert to use for chartering yachts in Europe (cost $150)
•.     These courses are conducted along the WA coast between Busselton & the Abrolhos Islands.  
• More information on this course [HERE](https://www.iytworld.com/courses/international-flotilla-skipper/)

***Option 3 International Bareboat Skipper*** 
•    VHF radio licence required.
•    Must have completed 200 nm and 10 days at sea (By the end of the course) to qualify for 
this qualification.
•    This qualification can be converted to an ICC certificate to use for chartering yachts in 
Europe. (cost $150)
•    More information on this course [HERE](https://www.iytworld.com/courses/international-bareboat-skipper/)

##WHAT YOU NEED TO DO NOW:
Please complete these steps before joining your Adventure Sailing Course.
 
1.	***Register at IYT World*** [Here]( https://iytnet.com/index.php?option=com_content&view=featured&Itemid=101)
•	This is needed for issue of your certificate. Record your student number and bring it with you. 
•	It also allows you access to LOTS of FREE e learning material. A little pre study will result in greater learning during your course. 

2.	***Select required course*** 

##What to bring:
Everything is provided on board you simply need to bring the following: 

- 1 X Passport Photo. (If doing your radio licence) 
- Clothes for 5 days (include some warm clothes)
- Sunglasses & Hat (that can stay on in the wind!)
- Wet weather jacket (we can lend you one of ours if you wish) 
- Head torch 
- Shoes that can get wet for exploring the coast. 
- Bathers (and wetsuit if you wish)
- A good book and camera
- Towel
- Secret snacks & lollies!
- Alcohol (if you wish)
- Toiletries
- Water bottle 

Please pack into a SOFT bag only, no suitcases. We have limited storage space. 

##What NOT to bring:
- Baby wipes (these are the worst marine toilet blockers, and a blocked toilet is no fun for anyone) There will be plenty of opportunities to swim and wash. 

Please note. The only shower onboard is a manual deck shower. Saltwater soap is provided. 


##Frequently asked questions:

1. ***What qualifications can we get?*** 
We can offer you, at the successful passing of the exam, 3 qualifications at the end of this course. International Yacht Training, International bareboat skippers’ qualification.
International certificate of competency http://www.iytworld.com
Short range operators’ certificate of proficiency. (VHF radio Licence) 

2. ***Is there any online training available prior to joining Queimarla?*** 
We will provide you with a comprehensive “e course” that you can work through in the comfort of your own home prior to sailing with us. 
You will also receive an “e copy” of the IYT textbook for your course. 
We will also send you a series of links to online u tube clips that we think are knowledgeable and worth watching. 

3. ***What is your rough weather contingency plan?*** 
We place your safety above all other considerations. 
Queimarla is a remarkable sea boat that has successfully sailed around the world. She is strong, safe and is fully approved by AMSA. We do not take undue risk; however, we do not hide from a little rough weather. This is your opportunity to stretch your envelope of comfort whilst having a lifelong professional sailor onboard with you. 
Saying this we can fly home from the Abrolhos Islands if caught out there by extreme weather. 

4. ***Can we fish onboard?*** 
This is predominately a sailing trip, but we certainly tow a lure when able and have a fish at anchor. We do not bring fish home; we eat what we catch onboard. You must make sure you have a current [WA Recreational Fishing license](https://www.fish.wa.gov.au/Fishing-and-Aquaculture/Recreational-Fishing/Pages/Recreational-Fishing-Licences.aspx) if you wish to spear fish, dive for crays or fish. 
 
5. ***Can we surf?*** 
We have no insurance for surfing. 

6. ***What about Diving?*** 
We would be crazy not to enjoy this incredible environment into which we are sailing. Yes, to snorkelling, yes to insurance, yes to we have gear onboard. 

7. ***What gear is onboard?*** 
- All safety gear including life jackets & harnesses.
- All bedding.
- All Food and cooking equipment.
- Fridge & Freezer.
- Sunscreen.
- Snorkelling gear
- SUP board.
- 3.75m dinghy.
- Basic fishing gear.
- 2 x SUP boards & paddles.
- All training resources and equipment. 
- Blue tooth speaker.
- Manual deck shower only
- Salt water soap.

8. ***Do we need to study?*** 
We get 3 different sorts of people onboard: Those that want the awesome experience, those that want to be able to sail a charter boat and need the qualifications and those that want to sail their own boats and adventures. 
Which are you? The last two groups should do some pre-study as provided. This will deepen your learning. The first group can mix another piña colada and observe!

9. ***Do I have to get the certificates?*** 
IYT charge $150 per certificate. You need them if chartering, they may reduce your insurance premium or make insurance easier to get and they look great in the pool room, but the choice is yours. 

10. ***Is there a hot shower?*** 
We spend a great deal of effort keeping water out of the boat, so there is no shower below decks. We do have a saltwater deck shower, saltwater soap available and a freshwater rinse down on deck. We try to swim every day and so far, we have had no complaints about our smell. 
*Please DO NOT bring baby wipes or body wipes.* These things are an environmental disaster and the most prevalent blockers of marine toilets ever invented. They should be illegal. 
Swimming in the blue ocean is a perfect way to stay clean and fresh. We will have biodegradable salt water soap that works a treat. 

11. ***What is the food like?*** 
I really like food. Lots of delicious fresh food. You will eat well and be part of the crew preparing these delicious meals. This can get a little competitive and result in some spectacular outcomes. You won’t be disappointed. 

12. ***How do we get to the boat?*** 
We mostly sail from Fremantle, Busselton, and Port Denison (Dongara). Travel to the boat is your responsibility. Some folk drive, some catch the Trans West bus. (Cheap and efficient) We have no secure parking available in Dongara. However, we have never had an issue. Yet. 

13. ***Coffee and Tea?***
We will have a selection of teas available on board, and fresh coffee beans. We have a hand crank coffee grinder, plungers and an Aeropress. It's a coveted job grinding the morning brew whilst standing up on deck staring at the water!


##HOW TO ACCESS FREE E-LEARNING COURSES FROM IYT##
1.	Log onto [IYTworld](https://iytnet.com)
2.	Sign in. (Must be signed into access courses)
3.	Along the top of the home page select COURSES
4.	Scroll down to IYT e Learning
5.	Select desired course. Eg International bareboat skipper’s course.
6.	Scroll to bottom of Introduction paragraph. Click HERE.
7.	Add to cart. (don’t worry it is FREE, you won’t be charged but you need to proceed through the checkout)
8.	Follow the prompts to the END of checkout.
9.	Accept terms of conditions.
10.	FINISHED
11.	You will receive an email confirming purchase. Course found at top of page under DASHBOARD tab. (MY E LEARNING COURSES)
.
All courses are available to you as a member of IYT.

##Suggestions to help you study for your course onboard.##
•	International crew for 3 day courses
•	International bareboat skipper for 5 day courses
•	Vhf short range certificates for radio licence.
###DON’T SIT THE EXAMS WE WILL DO THEM ONBOARD QUEIMARLA.###

If your specific questions have not been answered here please give Paul a call to discuss. 
0458772581 


Please read the following document. Fill in form and send back to Paul:
[5 Day trip Information Pack.pdf](https://cdn.filestackcontent.com/gCYHrMRLTsmStSmJGj1n)
paul@adventuresailing.com.au

For more info or questions **please do not reply to this email** as we won't see it! 
Instead email us at [paul@adventuresailing.com.au] (paul@adventuresailing.com.au)

Our mountain bikes are suited to different riders and terrains. Hire is available for up to four hours, letting you explore local trails, parklands or urban routes. Bikes are suitable for casual riders wanting an leisurely ride as well as more adventurous cyclists seeking off-road capability.
Whether you want a relaxed spin or a more technical ride, choose the bike that matches your comfort and ability, and enjoy independent exploration at your own pace.
Our bikes are well-maintained and suitable for a range of abilities, making this a great option for individuals, couples, groups, corporates and families.
A pre-ride briefing and trail guidance are provided to help you make the most of your ride.
Bike trails we operate on

Waikato River Trail - View www.waikatorivertrails.co.nz
Hauraki Rail Trail - View www.haurakirailtrail.co.nz
Timber Trail - View www.timbertrail.nz

Private lessons are great a great option if you'd like to further advance your surfing skills! Each session is 2 hours long and includes 1.5 hours of intensive one on one training, followed by a 30min free surf session on the equipment provided so you can practise what you've learnt. You can also book up x8 people in a private lesson so will work well if you have friends and family that would like to join.
If you've been struggling on a specific element in your surfing then these lessons will really help!
Cost:
$199 for 1-2 students
$299 for 3 students
$65 add extra students
Booking fees can be avoided by calling 0211764073
Duration:
2 Hours
Beginner Private Class (Option 1)
Beginner classes will focus on all the important fundamentals you should know before hitting the water by yourself E.g. beach safety, body positioning, basic pop up techniques, catching waves in the white water and more. After taking a few classes we highly recommend students do some practise rentals to practise by them selves.
Intermediate Private Classes (Option 2)
Intermediate classes will focus on riding unbroken waves, how to get through the waves properly, correct positioning to catch unbroken waves, how to turn and ride across the wave, advance pop up techniques and much more! These classes are suitable for students who have taken at least 2-3 beginner classes, had some practise by them selves and are feeling confident with their pop up in white water.
What’s Included:
1.5 hours of one on one private coaching
An extra 30min of free practise time after your lesson on the equipment provided
Surfboard and wetsuit
Video Analysis when required
x1 ISA (International Surfing Association) approved coach
Age:
Available for students 5 years and older
Please note for less experienced children who are part of a group booking we may require a parent to assist this child whilst the instructor works with the other people in the group.
If you have any questions or concerns then please call us on 0211764073 to discuss before making your booking.
Location:
Otaki Beach
Booking fees can be avoided by calling 0211764073

New Year’s Eve is fast approaching, and we hope you are as excited as we are about being on beautiful Sydney Harbour to experience the world’s most iconic fireworks display. 

With all the hustle and bustle that New Year’s Eve offers, please find some valuable information below to help make your boarding process easier.

##Your Vessel

Your cruise is on our vessel **Ocean Adventurer**. Please take the time to look at the image of your vessel below as Darling Harbour is a very busy area on New Year’s Eve and there will be many vessels departing on the night.

![Ocean Adventurer](https://assets.myfastferry.com.au/images/2021/12/30131942/33m.jpg)

##Departure Times

- The departure time of your **9pm Fireworks Cruise** is **19:15** sharp from **Darling Harbour – Pier 26, Berth 8**. 
- The departure time of your **Midnight Fireworks Cruise** is **22:15** sharp from **Darling Harbour – Aquarium Wharf**. 

## Check In

- Please check in at least **120 minutes prior to your scheduled departure time** 
- Please bring a **printed or digital copy of your booking confirmation** and check in with one of our team
- At check in you will receive a **boarding wristband** for your cruise.
- **Check in is available at the Fantasea Cruising Office from 12:00 on Wednesday, 31st December.**

##Check in location is the Fantasea Cruising Darling Harbour Office at Pier 26 (Directly underneath Helm Bar)

![Darling Harbour](https://www.fantasea.com.au/wp-content/uploads/sites/1538/2025/12/dh_office_map.jpg)
 
## Fraud Prevention

Please present the credit card that was used to pay for your booking and matching valid photo identification. The name listed on your credit card should match the name listed on your booking.

##Boarding

Please make your way to your departure wharf at least 45 minutes before your scheduled departure time. Fantasea Cruising staff will be on location to manage the queue and may allow less mobile passengers to move to the front.


##What to Bring

- You are welcome to bring along snacks and meals. Some snacks will be available for purchase onboard.
- **No BYO alcohol allowed**. There is a licensed bar on board for alcoholic beverages and soft drinks
- Appropriate clothing for the weather conditions on the night
- Please bring a **printed or digital copy of your booking confirmation** as you may need to show this to security personnel at various access points around Darling Harbour.

##On the Night

More than a million people will be making their way into the city for the celebrations. Please find details on road closures and public transport on New Year’s Eve below to help you plan your night.

- [**Public Transport**](https://www.sydneynewyearseve.com/transport)
- [**Road Closures**](https://www.sydneynewyearseve.com/road-closures/)

We very much look forward to having you on board with us to enjoy what promises to be one of the most spectacular events of the year!

Kind Regards,

The Fantasea Cruising / My Fast Ferry team

A special hosted Birthday Party at Urimbirra Wildlife Park will be sure to create lasting memories.
You can set up in our undercover or picnic areas, before the Park opens - while we take your guests on a fantastic adventure - a private meet and greet with the Koalas, feeding our noisy Rainbow Lorikeets and then on to a fun activity trail around the park interacting with our friendly animals and playing some games along the way!
A special "Party with the Animals" tshirt is available as an optional extra, for the Birthday Person - or the whole group! Minimum booking 6 children and 1 adult.
Sundays 9.30am start. Session is 2hours duration.
meta_raw_booking_notes:
Hi, 

Thanks for booking your birthday party at Urimbirra Wildlife Park! We look forward to sharing this day with you and creating some fantastic life long memories!

The session starts at 9.30am (before the Park opens at 10am) Mandy will greet you and give you access to set up in our Barbecue/Picnic area. Please ask the guests to arrive by 9.20am so we are ready to enter the Park at 9.30am. Any late comers will need to wait outside the Park (with their parent/guardian) until Mandy can go back and collect them. 

Only Booked in participants will be allowed access before 10am. 

Unbooked guests (parents/family) will need to pay upon entry at 10am.

The Birthday program is fairly flexible and is tailored to each group -It will include meeting, interacting and handfeeding our wide range of animals - from chickens, guinea pigs, sheep,and alpacas to quokkas, emus, koalas and kangaroos. and a very special feeding session with our very friendly rainbow lorikeets! As well as some animal related games and other fun activities.

Photos taken during the session will be available via our private Facebook Group - Urimbirra Programs. These could also feature on our social media pages - please let us know if you wish this NOT to occur.

We will arrive back to the Barbecue area at about 11.30 - and the children usually have built up an appetite! The Hosted part of the Program finishes at 11.30 - but you are more than welcome to stay on, have some lunch and go back out into the Park for another walk if you like. Children must be supervised by an adult. Please remember to be quiet and respectful around our animals - so that all will have an enjoyable time! 

Don't leave any food unattended - our Kangaroos and peacocks have been known to be quite resourceful!

Parents will need to pick up their Children at your designated time. Please ask your guests parents to wait in the car park area when picking up their child There is an area to the right of the Entrance door - marked by a traffic cone- that allows space for them to gather safely - as the area inside the shop can become congested.

Parents can not enter the park to pick up their children

We would also appreciate the area being left neat and tidy - with any rubbish placed in the bins provided. 

Thanks so much for your cooperation - please let me know if you have any questions

Cheers,

Mandy

Comfortable bush camping, great dining, fantastic service and wildlife encounters!
Duration
3 Days
About
Our most popular trip. Using top quality equipment and accredited, qualified guides, this trip covers 40 to 55 kilometres of wildlife rich river, downstream from Katherine and away from the often crowded Nitmiluk National Park (Katherine Gorge). Fed by springs and soaks throughout the long ‘Dry Season’, the river below the Gorge, winds through rocky banks, paperbark forests, small rapids and pandanus channels. Comfortable bush camping, great dining, fantastic service and wildlife encounters – it all adds up to being a unique experience. A trip you will never forget.
Itinerary
Day 1 - You will be met at your Katherine accommodation between 7-7:30am (0700-0730). You will then be transferred in a 4WD vehicle to Gecko premises, where you will pack your personal effects required for the tour into waterproof bags. You will be fitted with Personal Flotation Devices (PFD) a requirement, to be worn whilst on the river.
You will then be transferred to the Katherine River in a 4WD vehicle, sometimes over un-made roads and tracks. A safety brief and paddling instructions for kayaking and canoeing will be given before entering the water. At a relaxing rate, there will be stops along the river for a morning break, lunch, swim and time to view the diverse river environment, bird and wildlife. Approximately 4pm (1600) you will step ashore for an overnight remote camping experience (no set campsites). There will be time to relax; fish or read all whilst your guide prepares the evening meal. After a campfire meal, enjoyed with your favourite bottle of wine or spirit, sleep in a bed-roll (swag) under a blanket of stars.
Day 2 - Wake to a dawn chorus in the brisk morning air. There is time for an early morning swim. After a hearty cooked breakfast, we pack-up camp and continue paddling down-stream. As we get further from immediate civilisation, the feel of remoteness sets in. The river continues to change from shady paperbark forests to lush pandanus channels, through open sections, surrounded by the river woods and over some small sparkling rapids which are fun and easy to negotiate. At the end of this satisfying day, you will find yourself in a bit of a routine and will have camp set-up quickly. Leaving yourself enough time to explore, relax, chat , check-out some animal tracks or just ‘find yourself’.
Day 3 - After a sumptuous breakfast, we will pack up camp for the last time (you will now know where everything goes), we will return to the kayaks for one last relaxing day. You will be ‘tuned in’ to all the sights and sounds around you and will find yourself exhilarated by every experience, enjoy it while the moment lasts. At approximately 2:30pm (14:30) you will be picked up from the river and transferred in a 4WD back to Gecko premises to collect your belongings. You will then be transferred to your Katherine accommodation or bus terminal as per prior arrangements made. Tour end 5:30pm approximately.
More info
The Canoes/Kayaks
We use a range of ‘Scupper Pro’ sit-on-top kayaks or 2 person canoes, (mainly for adult/child or couple pairing). The sit on tops are self draining, comfortable and very stable. The canoes are 4.5m open style polypropelene suited for touring. Many of our guests have never paddled before. Our fully qualified and accredited guides ensure that this is not a problem.
Where We Stop
We are totally self sufficient giving us the luxury of being selective with our campsites and resting points along the river. There’s plenty of time to relax, swim, fish, bird watch, encounter wildlife and appreciate the scenery. We regularly access these sites with group sizes of 2-8, ensuring that we have minimal impact on the environment.
How Far, How Long, When?
Typically, a 3 day trip can cover up to 50km of river. Paddling down stream, there is minimal portaging of equipment. Tours operate during the ‘TOP END’ dry season, May to September. The temperature ranges from 24 C to 39 C, but the nights from June to August can be cool, dropping to 8 degrees Celsius.
Tour accommodation
We are fully self-sustained while on tour, giving us the ability to stop and set camp, wherever we wish.
You are Supplied With
- Canvas bedroll, ‘we call it a swag’ – for those who wish to sleep outside
- A ‘Thermarest’ self inflating mattress
- Sleeping bag which can be fully opened
- Liner (or sheet) and pillow, a torch & mosquito repellent
The Campsites
Exclusive to us and well equipped. It includes:
- Dining Tables and chairs (with back rests)
- Cooking Grill, Kettle & Camp ovens
- Riverside views and swimming spots
- A shovel and toilet paper (for the call of nature)
We bring out our rubbish; bury human waste 100m from water and burn toilet paper in the fire.
The Meals
Always a surprise for the nature enthusiasts! All hearty home style fresh food. Dinners and breakfasts are cooked on an open fire
Lunches are ‘sandwich’ or ‘wrap’ style with cold meat and salad
A good old ‘Billy of Tea’ is available at lunch
Tea, Coffee and Hot chocolate are available at camp
The guide will do the washing up (unless you really want to help)
What to bring
We recommend that you pack lightly and limit the space required. A packing list will be provided for you. You are able to bring along a bottle or two of your favourite dinner wine. We have no space for cold drinks such as beer or soft drinks. For your personal gear we provide;
- A 20 litre water proof bag (for your clothes)
- A 10 litre water proof bag (for camera etc)

A fantastic opportunity to experience the Jatbula Trail and this remote and significant Savanna River of the ‘Top End’!
Duration
9 Days
About
This Tour starts and ends in Darwin. A fantastic opportunity to experience the Jatbula Trail and this remote and significant Savanna River of the ‘Top End’ in the Katherine Region 9 Day Jatbula and Katherine River Discovery Tour’-Waterfalls, Rivers, Wildlife, and Aboriginal Rock-art sites.
Trekking – part 1
On the famous 'Jatbula Trail', 5 days Bushwalking through the remote stone country of the Jawoyn Peoples ‘Nitmiluk National Park’, along a traditional (Aboriginal) 'Message Stick' trail, which passes by Rock-art sites from the Katherine River to Edith Falls in Nitmiluk National Park
Kayaking – part 2
Using top quality equipment and qualified, accredited guides, this trip covers up to 50 kilometres of intimate river. Fed by springs and soaks year round, the river winds through rocky banks, paperbark forests, small sparkling rapids and pandanus channels. Wildlife encounters, comfortable ‘swag style’ camping, great dining, fantastic service, – it all adds up to being a unique experience. A trip you may never forget.
Day 1 - 7:00AM pick-up from Darwin. We stop for a leg stretch (and coffee) enroute. You will arrive in Katherine in time to take an optional boat cruise in the magnificent Nitmiluk Gorge. Tonight we camp nearby Nitmiluk National Park at our basic ‘but private’ bush camp, providing dinner and time to make sure that all your equipment is in working order before heading out on the trail.
Day 2 - Hiking approx 8.2kms.
We leave our camp at 7 am approximately, where you will be transferred to Nitmiluk National Park and the 5 day walking trail, here you will catch a boat across to the mouth of the Seventeen Mile Creek where your trail begins.
Hiking into Northern Rock hole for Morning Tea allows time to adjust backpacks and hiking boots before they get too uncomfortable. Take a rest in the shade, drink some cool water and then continue onto camp at Biddlecombe Cascades where there will be time for a relaxing soak in some of the scenic and shaded rock pools.
Day 3 - Hiking approx 11.3kms.
After starting early – always good to get going on sunup – we continue on our way to Edith Falls. Today we will see the first of our Rock Art paintings, sheltered by an amazing rock formation; we will spend Morning Tea, again resting our backs and feet before moving onto camp at Crystal Falls. Crystal Creek is a great place to get out and stretch the body in the huge waterhole right beside the camp.
Day 4 – Hiking approx 10.1kms.
Another early start gets us to the Crystal Falls Lookout first thing for a sunrise, then we move onto the Amphitheatre for Morning Tea where we can leave our packs behind for 40 mins and descend into the cool monsoon forest to explore for more Rock Art, or maybe just sit in the shade and enjoy the serenity. Camp tonight is at the top of 17 Mile Falls, a walk to the bottom can be arranged, or you can just relax at the top of the falls in one of the cool and scenic pools.
Day 5 – Hiking approx 18kms.
Setting off at sunrise will give us time to get to the Edith River Crossing for a late Morning Tea/Early Lunch. Again a great place to take off the backpack and let the feet relax for a while. After our break we arrive at camp for the evening, a place called Sandy Billabong. Here you can swim or spa, a great place for bird watching in the afternoon, and the pool provides amazing reflection shots as the afternoon sky changes colour.
Day 6 – Hiking 15kms.
One more early start will get us through some long grass, across a couple of creeks and through a bog all in time to have lunch at Sweetwater Pool. This is another amazing place to have a rest and contemplate why we do what we do! After leaving here it is but a mere 5kms more to Edith Falls where we can take the scenic lookout walk back to the kiosk where a cold drink and an ice cream will be waiting for us. We will be picked up at 3:00PM and head back to Katherine, you will be back in time to unpack and repack then return to our private campground again (or you can choose to stay at a Motel (at own cost).
Day 7 – You will be met at your Katherine accommodation between 7-7:30am (0700-0730). You will then be transferred to Gecko premises, where you will pack your personal effects required for the tour into waterproof bags. You will be fitted with Personal Flotation Devices (PFD) a requirement, to be worn whilst on the river.
You will then be transferred to the Katherine River in a 4WD vehicle, sometimes over un-made roads and tracks. A safety brief and paddling instructions for kayaking and canoeing will be given before entering the water. At a relaxing rate, there will be stops along the river for a morning break, lunch, swim and time to view the diverse river environment, bird and wildlife. Approximately 4pm (1600) you will step ashore for an overnight remote camping experience (no set campsites). There will be time to relax; fish or read all whilst your guide prepares the evening meal. After a campfire meal, enjoyed with your favourite bottle of wine or spirit, sleep in a bed-roll (swag) under a blanket of stars.
Day 8 – Wake to a dawn chorus in the brisk morning air. There is time for an early morning swim. After a hearty cooked breakfast, we pack-up camp and continue paddling down-stream. As we get further from immediate civilisation, the feel of remoteness sets in. The river continues to change from shady paperbark forests to lush pandanus channels, through open sections, surrounded by the river woods and over some small sparkling rapids which are fun and easy to negotiate. At the end of this satisfying day, you will find yourself in a bit of a routine and will have camp set-up quickly. Leaving yourself enough time to explore, relax, chat , check-out some animal tracks or just ‘find yourself’.
Day 9 - After a sumptuous breakfast, we will pack up camp for the last time (you will now know where everything goes), we will return to the kayaks for one last relaxing day. You will be ‘tuned in’ to all the sights and sounds around you and will find yourself exhilarated by every experience, enjoy it while the moment lasts. At approximately 2:30pm (14:30) you will be picked up from the river and transferred in a 4WD back to Gecko premises to collect your belongings. You will then be transferred to your Katherine accommodation as per prior arrangements made. Tour end 5:30pm approximately. We will provide a transfer from your accommodation to the transit centre.
Day 10 - We will transfer you to the Katherine Visitor Centre where you can have a refreshment. The centre is across the road from the transit centre, you can walk across to board your return bus back to Darwin.
More info
Meals and Accommodation: 1 night Motel, 1 night Private Bush-Camp, and 6 nights remote bush-camping, that is, no facilities (except our own self sustaining equipment), camped under the stars at secluded riverside camps.
Evening meals, if you choose to book in a Katherine Motel are not provided, so that you may have your choice of where and when, you want to eat.
The Canoes/Kayaks
We use a range of ‘Scupper Pro’ sit-on-top kayaks or 2 person canoes, (mainly for adult/child or couple pairing). The sit on tops are self draining, comfortable and very stable. The canoes are 4.5m open style polypropelene suited for touring. Many of our guests have never paddled before. Our fully qualified and accredited guides ensure that this is not a problem.
Where We Stop
We are totally self sufficient giving us the luxury of being selective with our campsites and resting points along the river. There’s plenty of time to relax, swim, fish, bird watch, encounter wildlife and appreciate the scenery. We regularly access these sites with group sizes of 2-8, ensuring that we have minimal impact on the environment.
The Jatbula Trail is located within the boundaries of Nitmiluk National Park, following the Seventeen Mile Valley from Nitmiluk Gorge to Edith Falls. The local Flora and Fauna is prolific and the scenery is varied and beautiful. The Katherine River, Seventeen Mile Creek and the Edith River flow all year round and during the long drty-season, become the only water sources for all manner of wildlife. The Katherine Region is a terrific place to visit and base your Northern Territory experience from. We are close to The Kimberley, Gregory National Park, Elsey National Park, Manyallaluk, Kakadu Heritage Area and of course, right on our doorstep, is the magnificent Katherine/Flora/Daly River System.
Where We Stop
We are totally self sufficient giving us the luxury of being selective with our resting points, campsites however are designated due to the status of the National Park. There’s plenty of time to relax, swim, bird watch, encounter wildlife and appreciate the scenery. We regularly access these sites with group sizes of 2-8, ensuring that we have minimal impact on the environment. On the trail we are sharing sites with other hikers, numbers on the trail are generally small allowing groups to spread out and have their own area.
Tour Accommodation
We are fully self-sustained while on the trail. While hiking we stop at designated camping sites. If not providing your own equipment, You are provided with:
You are Supplied With
-Tent on walk and a Canvas bedroll on the river, ‘we call it a swag’ – for those who wish to sleep outside
- A self inflating mattress
- Sleeping bag which can be fully opened
- Liner (or sheet) and pillow, a torch & mosquito repellent
The Campsites
Fixed campsites on the jatbula Trail and on river they are exclusive to us and well equipped.River trip includes:
- Dining Tables and chairs (with back rests)
- Cooking Grill, Kettle & Camp ovens
- Riverside views and swimming spots
- A shovel and toilet paper (for the call of nature)
We bring out our rubbish; bury human waste 100m from water and burn toilet paper in the fire.
While we are on the hiking tour we forgo chairs and tables along with grills and camp ovens. We cook with small fuel burning stoves allowing us to have hot meals and hot drinks throughout the tour.
The Meals
- Breakfasts consist of cereals/porridge/oatmeal
- Dinners are typical light weight meals cooked on a fuel stove
- Lunches are ‘sandwich’ or ‘wrap’ style (normally crisp breads)
- Tea, Coffee and Hot chocolate are available at camp
- The guide will do the washing up (unless you really want to help)
What to bring
We recommend that you pack lightly and limit the space required. A packing list will be provided for you. For your personal gear we can provide;
A 65-75 litre backpack, (ruck sack), or you may wish to use your own. You will only need minimal clothing – you can rinse items out daily. Keep things as light and small as possible to compensate for food & water, a headlamp or torch (spare batteries) and personal first aid kit.

About
Join WAM on our epic 5 day Great Alpine & Lakes Adventure in the Victorian Alps & Gippsland Lakes.
From Skiing & Snowboarding Mount Hotham, Australia’s highest alpine village, snowshoeing to eco villages for dinner, driving the iconic Great Alpine Road, kayaking the Gippsland Lakes, bathing in the Metung Hot Springs with lake vistas, whale watching cruise at Wilsons Prom, and tasting fantastic produce along the way with a small group of likeminded legends.

meta_raw_booking_notes:
Thanks for choosing this Great Alpine & Lakes winter adventure with WAM! We can't wait for you to join us on a spectacular journey into the Victorian Alps and Gippsland Lakes.

As one of Australia's only certified tour operator B-Corps, just by booking with us, you have done a lot of good for the planet, congratulations! (read on for more details of how)

Before we do so, please take a minute to read some important information about the trip:

- For our Great Alpine & Lakes Adventure, we require a minimum of 5 people for the trip to run. If the trip does not reach minimum numbers, we will inform you at least 60 days prior to the trip and you will be provided with a full refund of what you have paid.
- The balance of the trip is due 60 days before departure.
- You’ll start receiving emails as we get closer to the date with information about the trip, what to bring etc.
- Once you have the date confirmed, if you need to cancel, we require a minimum 60 days notice to provide a refund (less your deposit)


##Pick up Location
We will have 3 pick-up locations on the day of departure.
Mornington Peninsula
Frankston
Melbourne CBD
We will provide further details on these closer to the date.

##Equipment hire and lessons - Mount Hotham
- We can help arrange equipment hire and lessons at Mount Hotham if required so please contact us for further details.

##Premium Service
- To maximise your comfort we provide you with an eco-pack for the trip which includes products from Australian businesses that directly support the environment. This includes a reusable water bottle, keep-cup, reef-safe sunscreen, sunscreen and a towel. You simply hand these back at the end of your experience. Its a bit like a pack you may get on a first class flight or a luxury hotel, except ours is good for the planet!

##Now for the deep and meaningful:
By booking an adventure with us you have directly helped make a long-term positive environmental and social impact by:

- Donating a portion of everything booking to Zoos Victoria to support the Mountain Pygmy Possum (and other endangered species), these little guys were thought to be extinct until being discovered in a loft in Hotham in the 1960's. Critically endangered, Mountain Pygmy Possums are Australia's only hibernating marsupial so will be sleeping while we are on the slopes above, knowing we have supported the conservation of this very special species. 

- Planting native trees on the Mornington Peninsula with MP Koalas to capture carbon emissions, protect our climate, enhance soil and water quality, and restore habitat for native wildlife. 
- Regenerate reefs and native kelp locally with The Nature Conservancy, providing marine habitat, filtering seawater, removing nitrogen and phosphate, and preventing used shell from entering landfill.
- Support female education with The Stars Foundation which empowers and supports Indigenous young women and girls to complete education and find work.
- Protect and plant mangroves to protect our coastlines, wildlife and support blue carbon projects.

You'll find additional information relevant to your adventure on the Wild Adventures Melbourne website. Please check the website for exactly what items we recommend bringing with you on the day.

##Green is our Gold Commitment:

As members of Australia’s tourism industry, we believe a land as precious
as ours should be preserved for generations to come. As a visitor, we ask that you do the same. That’s why we’ve set some unwritten rules that have kept our backyard beautiful for thousands of years.

Passed down through story and practice, they’re how we walk gently, listen deeply, tread with care – and look out for each other along the way. 

By following them throughout your visit, you too can care for Australia when you Come and say G’day.

Consider these principles a bit of local knowledge. A few fundamentals to help you respect this place and have an unforgettable stay in the process.

The Guiding Principles:

Celebrate Community
The best part of an Australian visit is the people you meet.
Shop local, engage with communities, and you’ll leave with new mates aplenty.

Embrace Culture
Australia’s cultural diversity stretches from ancient songlines to city laneways. Immerse yourself in it all - honour First Nations cultures, embrace our diversity, and you’ll leave with new knowledge and new friends.

Preserve Place
In Australia you’ll find some of the most unspoilt landscapes on Earth. Help keep them that way by minimising your impact wherever you go.

Respect Wildlife
Australia has some of the most unique animals on the planet. Take as many photos as you like but remember to give them space and respect their homes.

Take Care
We look out for one another in Australia, but it’s important to take care of yourself too. Listen to the land, respect it, and always put safety first.


If you have any questions between now and your trip with us, please don't hesitate to email or call me directly.

Looking forward to adventuring with you soon,

Nic 'Coops' Cooper
WAM Founder

Knowledge Development (online, home study or in a classroom) to understand basic principles of scuba diving,
Confined Water Day to learn basic scuba skills
2 Shore Dives on Day 2 to build on your skills

Thank you for joining Sydney Kayak on a day Paddle adventure.
Your guide for this adventure is Sam Mcleod

##Schedule:
Meet at the boat ramp in the Tench Reserve 9.30am. Please be on time. We will
pack the Kayaks, have a safety and paddle technique briefing and plan to be on
the water by 10.00.
We usually stop for a break at Glenbrook Creek and lunch at either Euroka
Creek or Breakfast creek, depending on the speed and ability of the group.
On the trip home we stop again at Glenbrook Creek.

##What is supplied:
Sydney Kayak supplies the kayaks and kayaking equipment, Lunch and
Sunscreen.

##What to bring:
You should bring at least 1ltr of water per person, a change of clothes for after
the paddle in case you get wet. It is rare for anyone to fall in but you can get
damp from paddle splash.
You can bring phones and Cameras but remember there is a risk as they don’t
float and usually don’t work if dropped in water. For anything with a touch
screen it is a good idea to have a small cloth to wipe drops from wet fingers off
the screen as they can be sensed as a finger touch and make use difficult.
Anything you don’t want to get wet should be in a zip lock bag or dry bag.
There is very little room in a Kayak so back packs are best left behind unless
very small.

##What to wear:
Paddling is a water sport so expect to get splashed. Your feet will get wet. Footwear is strongly recommended.
The clothing Golden Rules - your kayak clothing should:
- NO COTTON or DENIM - when it gets wet, it does not dry and
remains cold and heavy! NOT EVEN JOCKS or socks!
- When wet it must stay warm AND dry quickly!
- The key concept to bear in mind is layering. Several thin garments will
keep you just as warm as a single thicker one, and are much more
versatile. Remember you’ll need to think about staying cool as much as
staying warm, and you can always add or subtract layers.
- A light Nylon Jacket will keep out wind and water. Fleeces are OK. Avoid heavy Jackets

##What to expect:
You will be paddling up the beautiful Nepean Gorge.
Most of this paddle is in the bush so there is a great assortment of birds and
wildlife to be seen. Being wildlife there are trips where we see a lot and other
times not as much.
Phone reception is non-existent on some of this paddle.
There are no toilets so, if needed, comfort stops will mean finding space behind
a friendly tree or rock.
Most people of average fitness who are non paddlers find they are tired but not
shattered. You are in doubles so you can share the workload.
Weather cancellation:
In the event of bad weather (rain or high winds) A decision will be made the
evening 36 hours before the paddle so for a Saturday paddle the decision will be
made Thursday evening. If you don’t receive a call or txt its going ahead.

##Directions:
We meet at the old boat ramp, (Next to New boat ramp, opposite the Coffee
club Café) Tench reserve, Tench Ave, Jamison town Penrith. Look for the
Kayaks on the old boat ramp.
Take the Mulgoa Rd exit off the M4.

meta_raw_booking_notes:
#Ahoy skipper,

**Please read all the following info carefully**

We are so excited to confirm your Early Riser booking with us!   
The picnic boat suits up to 7 people and is a quiet and calm way to see the Swan River. 

Further to our website info and our T&C’s that you have agreed to, we have gathered a few helpful bits of information to prepare you for a day on the boat.   

Our priority is your safety so there is a lot of learning prior to setting out on the river  

#Step 1. Pack a breakfast and wake up with the river

Starting the day on the river is magical. The boat has a large picnic table in the middle. Bring your own feast and drinks to enjoy on the boat. 
Pack lightly. Max 1 hard esky (60cm). Cooler bags can fit under the table, but please do not overload the boat.
You may want to bring a light jacket as some mornings can be crisp on the water.  

#Step 2. Know Before You Go

Your 2 hour hire starts at 7.45am with a 15min Safety Induction and by 8am you are setting off. You will return by 10am. Planning your trip is important. 

To see where you can sail, please click on our Sample Itinerary page and plan your journey prior to your boat hire day. Early Riser has its own map.

**MUST READ**   
[Itinerary](https://www.nautipicnics.com.au/itinerary/)	 	
[FAQ](https://www.nautipicnics.com.au/faq/)

#Step 3. You're the skipper, You're responsible

Choose your skipper carefully and prior to the hire day. **If you are not the skipper, please forward this email to your designated skipper so they can prepare** 
Even though you don’t need a skipper’s ticket, you do need to have a basic understanding of navigations and what you can and cannot do on the boat and the river 

A skipper means you are legally responsible for:
- The safety of our vessel and your passengers.
- Not endangering any other vessels.
- Must be ready to assist others who need help
- Checking if the weather is suitable for boating
- Understanding navigation rules and regulations on the river
- Staying sober with alcohol blood level of less than 0.05% 
- Being over 20 years old (children cannot be in control of the vessel)

**MUST READ** 
[Boat Safety](https://www.nautipicnics.com.au/boatsafety/)
[Safety Operation Manual](https://www.nautipicnics.com.au/s-o-m/)
**DOWNLOAD** [Nebo app](https://fleet.nebo.global/nautipicnics/public/a7e6e560-86e5-4b0c-886a-f94a8eeb5fe5?key=WTR60V5SD7VQ18IJ8X617JUNHE)

#Step 4. Weather Protection!!

Perth is subject to a range of weather conditions and sometimes the forecast can be wrong. As a boating company we rely heavily on the weather, especially for the wind gusts to be lower than 30km. We do not operate in high gusts, heatwaves (40+ degrees) or rain
Please keep up to date on the weather so you don't get surprised. 
Check the wind gusts at Ascot, East Perth and Bayswater to get a feel for the weather. 

**If you are travelling from**:
- another country or state, or  
- only want to use the boat for a special occasion,  we recommend you get the **weather protection** for $50.  

This will provide you with a full refund in case we have to reschedule due to unsuitable weather conditions. The protection fee is non refundable.

Just hit reply to this email if you would like to purchase the protection and we will deduct it straight from your credit card. It cannot be purchased after today!.

**MUST READ** [Weather](https://www.nautipicnics.com.au/weather-forecast-and-policy/)

#Step 5. Conduct - an unfortunate clause

There may be times when we consider it appropriate to refuse or prohibit passengers onboard our boat, or call you back from your hire earlier. 
These situations may be:
- not being prepared and is found to be unfit to control our boat
- inappropriate behaviour
- intoxication
- not following navigation rules and are putting your crew in danger 

You agree that this is our absolute right and refusal by any person on board to adhere to our request will result in an immediate cessation of the operation of the hire with no refund. You agree to be responsible for any guests brought onto the vessel and you agree to forfeit of any payment made to us in such circumstances.

**MUST READ** [Terms & Conditions](https://www.nautipicnics.com.au/t-c/)

#Step 6. Look out for your reminder email

In that email you will find out what you need to do on the day of your hire

That's all the formal stuff from us, for now. We'll be in touch again soon to see if there's anything else we can do to assist you during your hire.

If you have any questions, please let us know prior to your hire by replying to this email.
We look forward to you and your crew’s onboarding and we are certain you will have an unforgettable boating experience.

Fair Winds, 
Yvonne Larsen

**Nauti Picnics**

##Boarding

Please make your way to your departure wharf at least 45 minutes before your scheduled departure time. Fantasea Cruising staff will be on location to manage the queue and may allow less mobile passengers to move to the front.

- **No BYO alcohol allowed**. There is a licensed bar on board for alcoholic beverages and soft drinks

meta_raw_description: Join historian and archaeologist Elliot Lindsay on a thrilling walk from Circular Quay to Woolloomooloo, uncovering 12,000 years of Sydney’s hidden waterfront history. Wander past the Opera House, Botanic Gardens, Farm Cove and Mrs Macquarie’s Chair as you hear astonishing tales of 20-foot sharks, convict gangs, sailor riots, opium smugglers, Indigenous heroes, pioneering women, unsolved murders and the fiery destruction of the Garden Palace. Discover secret burials, forgotten carvings, bizarre legends and crime scenes tucked behind Sydney’s most iconic landmarks. A fascinating journey through beauty, mystery and mayhem—brought to life with vintage “then and now” photographs.

meta_raw_description:
The Event
When one thinks of suburbs like Killara, Gordon, Pymble and St Ives, found on Sydney's Upper North Shore, it is common to visualise beautiful houses, pretty gardens, flowering jacaranda trees, tennis courts and European cars.
However, long before golf, netball, and lawn bowls became the preferred pastimes, the region was notorious for blood sports, horse racing, violent blood feuds, frontier justice and murder!
Come on the ultimate evening of discovery with a glass of wine or beer and nibbles, at the historical Killara Golf Club. Listen to historian and archaeologist Elliot Lindsay tell the most incredible stories of long-forgotten events dating between 1820 and 1930. Illustrated with a presentation of stunning maps, illustrations and photographs.
You will hear about:
Battles with bushrangers.
The Killara Green Gate murder mystery.
Bare-knuckle boxing and cock fighting tournaments.
Naval battles on the Lane Cove River.
When the Rocks Push challenged the Waterhouse boys to a duel.
Peter Jackson, the legendary black heavyweight boxer who was trained at the Green Gate Hotel and became one of the world's greatest.
The Gordon murder mystery.
The Murder of Police Sargent Hickey on Pymble Golf Course. The long-forgotten pubs and gambling houses.
The Venue
The event will be held in the Killara Golf Club clubhouse—one of Australia's oldest golf clubs. Established in 1899, it is one of the few remaining relics from a quaint bygone era. The clubhouse building dates back to 1933 and exudes old-world charm. Very few non-members ever have the opportunity to experience and observe the splendid beauty of the historical institution.
A complimentary drink and nibbles with each ticket
Each ticket comes with one complimentary glass of house wine, beer or non-alcoholic beverage . There will also be charcuterie board nibbles served.
Transport
The club house plenty of parking. However, it is only a 13 minute walk from Killara Train Station.

#TOUR START

1. We’ll start at an iconic family-run deli forwith a coffee (or an iced cafe crema) and tasting of the house-made cheeses along with Australian olives and meats (kangaroo salami. ..yum!).

2. Next, its another Sydney icon and our most famous Banh Mi (Vietnamese pork roll).

Minimum Number of 25 students for any group Booking
The He Toi Tupu Education Tour is tailored to pre-school, primary, intermediate and secondary schools. This experience will take schools on a journey through one of New Zealand’s most significant Maaori earthwork fortifications of the 1860s.
The Rangiriri invasion by military forces is considered to be one of the bloodiest battles during the crown invasion of Waikato. This tour aligns with Aotearoa New Zealand's Histories and Te Takanga o te Waa and provides opportunities for teachers to engage in alternative methods to deliver their Histories curriculum. Through this experience, teachers, leaders and aakonga will gain a better understanding of a historical event that has impacted and shaped our present-day lives of Waikato and the Kiingitanga.
Walk through the world’s first Maaori replica earthwork trenches built to scale. Journey into the 19th century and learn about the Maaori spirit of resilience that led to the survival of Waikato and their ally tribes. Be moved by the narratives told by descendants of the men, women, and children who committed the ultimate act of selflessness. We survived annihilation and live to tell the stories.
The Experience
He Toi Tupu Education Tour includes visiting historic sites of significance including Te Maataarae ki Rangiriri (old paa site & military redoubt), the remnants of the original Rangiriri Paa earthworks and the world's first Maaori replica earthwork trenches built to its original scale. You will learn of the local narratives about the atrocities of the Waikato invasion and the stories behind the carved Pou (carved posts) and Tomokanga (carved entrances) carved by Kingitanga Master Carvers. meta_raw_description: Tuff Nutterz is a lively, family-friendly event centred on Australia’s biggest inflatable obstacle course, with climbing walls, slides, tunnels and other challenging features for kids and adults. The event also includes a giant 6m “Tuff Slide”, a miniature obstacle course, other carnival style inflatable games and appearances from the event mascot, Tuffy the dancing T-rex. Food and treats are available from an ice-cream trailer and food truck when on site. Sessions run across weekends and school-holiday dates to deliver a fun, active day out for families and groups.
meta_raw_booking_notes:
![Description of image](https://cdn.filestackcontent.com/7nrNEH9lR4aJzAf3Qt14)

We require **all visitors who are participating** in any of our activities to **sign a waiver** as, like with any high-intensity activity, it informs you of the risks involved. It also asks for a few things in return from you, as our guests, to keep yourselves, your group, and our staff safe. If participants are under the age of 18, a parent or legal guardian must sign the waiver on their behalf. Please **forward the waiver link to other parents/legal guardians in your group**.

The Waiver is to make sure you:

Understand and agree to abide by our safety rules
Agree to follow any rules or advice from our staff on site
Agree to make sure that any children you are responsible for abiding by our rules
Understand that you, and any children you are responsible for, participate at your own risk

**Once waivers are signed online just bring your booking QR Code either on your phone or hard copy (waivers will link to this) and make your way to the office to check in and get your wristbands. 

Please ensure you allow enough time for the check-in process. We recommend at least 30 minutes before the start of your session.

Late arrivals can join at any time, however, the end of your session will remain the same, as your session booked.

##Rules & Conditions of entry
All participants MUST have a signed waiver before entry.

Under 5’s require an accompanying parent/carer at ALL TIMES.

Adults MUST remain within the premises for all minors.

No food, no shoes, no sharp objects (including keys), no glasses, no glass, no jewellery, no candy, no gum, no mobile phones, no pets, no smoking, no alcohol or drugs or being under the influence of alcohol/drugs/medication.

No running, please take your time, no rushing or rushing others.

Allow plenty of space for the person in front of you.

ALWAYS look up whilst climbing. Do not climb underneath someone climbing above you. People can slip and fall whilst climbing. Use straps while climbing and take one step at a time.

No climbing or hanging from outside walls.

Make sure the landing area is clear of all people before jumping or sliding. Jump ONE at a time.

The correct sliding position on the slides is to have arms crossed across your chest with feet and legs together.

If sliding with another DO NOT hold hands. Slide separately.

Do not slide down any area that has climbing handles attached.

No pushing or rough play.

Smaller children should always be given right of way.

No tumbling or flipping and no diving.

Tread carefully and show caution as the course is uneven and spongy.

The course is only for use during public opening hours when obstacle course staff are on duty.

Obstacle Course staff directions must always be followed.

No medical conditions (Heart conditions, pregnancy, etc).Maximum weight 100Kg.

You may hear a whistle or megaphone announcement meaning stop and listen, wait for instructions in case of an emergency.

Enter at your own risk

##What to bring
Socks (preferably grip soles), water bottle (No glass), sunscreen, picnic blanket and some form of shade if needed.

Please bring your QR Code and signed online waivers, either on your phone or hard copy. Make your way to the ticket office to check in and get your wristbands. You can keep your wristband as a memento.

##What happens if it rains?

We won’t let wind or light rain stop the fun! For light rain, we recommend you bring a spare set of clothes. 
Take extra care if surfaces are slippery for instance due to the weather. It is recommended to wear socks with grip tread soles.
In the event of thunderstorms, heavy rain/winds or extreme weather conditions that could represent a risk we reserve the right to postpone, reschedule or cancel sessions or the event. We keep a close eye on the weather ahead of our events and will communicate any changes as soon as we can to ticket holders via email.
If an event session/day is cancelled/postponed on account of the weather, customers will be issued with a gift card to be used anytime in the future.

##Storage
Lockers are not available at the event, but you can leave your belongings at the ticket office with our staff if needed.

##Food & Drinks
We will have coffee, ice cream and yummy food available for purchase at our events.
You may bring your own food/drinks too. No alcohol is permitted.
No food or drinks are allowed on or near the inflatables. 
No glass is permitted on the premises for safety reasons.

##Check in
Please bring your QR Code and signed online waivers, either on your phone or hard copy. Make your way to the office to check in and get your wristbands. You can keep your wristband as a memento.
Please ensure you allow enough time for the check-in process. We recommend at least 30 minutes before the start of your session.
Late arrivals can join at any time, however, the end of your session will remain the same, as your session booked.

##Change of booking
Go to your confirmation email and find "change booking" below your booking date and time. Click on it and follow the process to change your booking.

meta_raw_description:
Get ready for an adrenaline-packed adventure that's about to take Fun to a whole new level
Tuff Nutterz is ready to unleash Australia's biggest inflatable adventure for the second time in Albury!. Get your heart racing as you conquer the twists, turns, and challenges of this exciting course, surrounded by the lush greenery of the garden. It's the ultimate family day out, where the young and young-at-heart can run, jump, and laugh their way through a whirlwind of fun. Don't miss out on the chance to make unforgettable memories and experience the thrill of Tuff Nutterz. So get your tickets, rally your crew, and prepare for an adventure like no other!
What's Tuff Nutterz all about? It's not just about the obstacles; it's about creating unforgettable memories for the whole family! You'll need to climb, slide, jump, and crawl your way to the finish line, all while having a blast with your family and friends.
Why You Can't Miss It - Tuff Nutterz isn't just an event; it's a celebration of togetherness, of pushing boundaries, and of pure, unadulterated fun! Whether you're a thrill-seeker or just looking for a fantastic day out with the family, Tuff Nutterz has something for everyone!
With Tuff Nutterz, there's no need to worry about age restrictions because the event welcomes all ages to participate and enjoy the fun. Parents with children under 5 years old are offered a special accompanying parent ticket .
So, gather your family and friends and get ready to tackle Australia's most exciting activity!!
Event dates & Opening hours
Sept 27th - Oct 1st - 9:00Am to 4:45Pm
Adress
393 Perry St, Albury NSW 2640
About
We tour the country bringing fun and excitement wherever we go. Some of the most iconic locations we've been to include Centennial Park, Darling Harbour, ICC, Parliamentary Triangle, Byron Bay and many more.
Ages
Suitable for all ages
Under 5’s require an accompanying parent/carer
Responsible adults MUST remain within the premises for all minors.
Important Ticket Info
Tickets can be purchased at the door, availability dependent. We strongly suggest booking online to avoid disappointment. Purchase the toddler ticket and an extra wristband will be automatically provided when you check-in at the event.
Only participants entering the actual inflatables need tickets. Spectators can remain on the premises without a ticket as long as they are not entering the games.
What happens if it rains?
We won’t let t rain stop the fun! We recommend you bring a spare set of clothes and towels. Take extra care if surfaces are slippery and wear socks with grip tread soles (You are welcome to re-schedule or request a gift-card if you don't want to participate in the rain).
In the event of thunderstorms, heavy rain/winds or extreme weather conditions that could represent a risk we reserve the right to postpone, reschedule or cancel sessions or the event. We keep a close eye on the weather ahead of our events and will communicate any changes as soon as we can to ticket holders via email.
If an event session/day is cancelled/postponed on account of the weather, customers will be issued a gift card to be used anytime in the future.
What to bring
Socks (preferably grip soles), water bottle (No glass), sunscreen, picnic blanket and some form of shade if needed.
Please bring your booking QR Code and signed online waivers, either on your phone or hard copy to help us speed up the check-in process. Make your way to the ticket office to check in and get your wristbands. You can keep your wristband as a memento.
Storage
Lockers are not available at the event, but you can leave your belongings safely with our staff at the ticket office, at no charge.
Food & Drinks
We will have coffee, ice cream and yummy food available for purchase at our events (availability dependent).
You may bring your own food/drinks too. No alcohol is permitted.
No food or drinks are allowed on or near the inflatables.
No glass is permitted on the premises for safety reasons.
Cancellation Policy
All sales are final, however, bookings can be re-scheduled or cancelled up to 24hs before your booking date. Go to your confirmation email and find "change booking" or "cancel booking" below your booking date and time. Click on it and follow the process to change your booking or to cancel and receive a gift card to rebook at your convenience.
In the case we need to cancel due to bad weather you will automatically receive a gift card to rebook for another day.
Didn't make it? Chill out, no shows will also be issued with a gift card upon request to come back another day.

Proudly part of the Balmain community since 1898.
General Information
Cost of Marquee Hire – 3hrs 30mins Period: $250
The hire fee covers the use of the marquee only.
You are welcome to use the adjacent turfed area for play activities such as jumping castles.
Please note: the turfed area is shared and available to all club patrons; it is not for exclusive use by marquee hirers.
Marquee Hire Information (3 Hours 30 Minutes Total)
• Your marquee booking is for a 3 hour and 30 minute period, plus an additional 30 minutes at the end allocated for pack-up and rubbish removal . Please ensure the space is cleared within this time, as another event may be scheduled immediately after yours.
• If you have booked a jumping castle, it must be removed within your allocated booking time , as the grass area needs to be cleared for the next event.
• For afternoon bookings , please note that a morning event may be scheduled prior, so early access may not be possible.
• All furniture must be returned to its original position before the end of your booking.
All food and drinks must be purchased from The Bistro. Food orders for functions must be prepaid in advance. No outside food or beverages are permitted, including water, soft drinks, chips, platters or snacks. The only exception is a birthday cake by prior arrangement. Any unauthorised outside food or beverages may incur a surcharge and be required to be removed from the premises .
Noise Policy
For evening functions held outside:
• No bands, DJs, or jukeboxes is not permitted after 10:00pm.
• Only light background music is allowed, kept at low volume, and must also cease at 10:00pm.
• Music inside the club for private functions is permitted until 10:00pm.
21st Birthday Parties
We love celebrating with you!
• Security hire is mandatory for 21st birthday parties and must be arranged at your own expense.
• You must confirm with us that security has been booked, or we can assist you in sourcing a licensed security guard.
• Failure to provide security on the day will result in cancellation of the event with no refund.
Cancellations
• Cancellations made more than two weeks prior to the booking date will receive a full refund.
• Cancellations made within two weeks of the booking date will receive a credit that can be used to rebook the Marquee at a later date.
• To cancel or inquire about a cancellation, please email us directly.
• No-shows will be charged the full hire fee.

🌴 Spirit Junior Island Cruise – Discover the Best of the Gold Coast
4-Hour Scenic Adventure You’ll Never Forget
9:30am - 1:30pm (Boarding at 9:00am)
Join us aboard Spirit Junior for a stunning 4-hour island cruise through the Gold Coast’s most beautiful waterways and island destinations. This small-group adventure combines breathtaking views, island exploring, swimming, wildlife encounters, and a delicious Aussie lunch — all in one unforgettable experience.
🏙️ Cruise the Gold Coast Skyline
Your journey begins with a relaxing cruise past the iconic Gold Coast skyline, where city meets sea. Sit back and take in the shimmering views as we make our way toward Wave Break Island, a local favourite for swimming only accessible by boat.
🌊 Swim & Explore Wave Break Island
We’ll drop anchor for an hour at Wave Break Island, the perfect spot to enjoy a refreshing swim in calm, crystal-clear waters. Relax on the beach or dive in for a splash — this island paradise is your playground.
🏝️ Island Hop to Tipplers via Sovereign Island
Next, we’ll cruise through the exclusive waterways of Sovereign Island, home to some of the Gold Coast’s most luxurious homes. Enjoy the scenery as we make our way to the famous Tipplers Bar & Café on South Stradbroke Island, a local gem surrounded by natural beauty.
🌿 Bushwalk & Wildlife Adventure
From Tipplers, embark on a gentle 900m bushwalk through lush coastal forest to a secluded surfside beach. Here, you’ll enjoy panoramic views of the Coral Sea and the chance to spot native wildlife including wallabies, echidnas, dolphins, dugongs, rays, turtles, marine birds and — if you’re lucky — the rare golden wallaby.
🍴 Aussie Lunch at Tipplers Café
Your cruise includes a freshly prepared Aussie-style lunch at Tipplers Café, with your choice of Fish & Chips, Calamari and Chips, BLTC (Vegetarian Option Available).
Prefer something different?
You can upgrade to the following for an additional $18 on the day:
Nachos with Avocado and Mexican Beef (Vegetarian Option Available)
Herb Crusted Hoki, Chips, Salad and Aioli
Tropical Chicken Burger with Chips
🚤 Scenic Return Cruise
After lunch, we’ll enjoy a leisurely return journey through the Broadwater, soaking in the peaceful waterways and coastal charm that make the Gold Coast so unique.
✨ Tour Details
Duration: 4 hours
Includes:
Scenic cruise aboard Spirit Junior
Island stop at Wave Break Island
Guided bushwalk and beach visit on South Stradbroke Island
Lunch at Tipplers Café
Wildlife spotting opportunities
Friendly, local crew
