Booking a fishing charter offers a unique and exciting experience, blending adventure with the tranquillity of being on the water
7 Hours
Before the Trip
Research and Selection:** Clients should carefully select a charter based on the type of fishing experience they desire, considering factors like location, type of fish targeted, boat size, and customer reviews.
Booking and Confirmation:** Once a charter is selected, clients will book their trip, and receive a confirmation detailing the trip date, duration, departure time, and location.
Preparation:** Clients will be informed of what to bring. This usually includes appropriate clothing, sun protection, and any personal fishing gear they prefer, however noting that adequate fishing gear is always supplied. We don’t supply food, however we have bottled water readily available.
Day of the Trip
Check-in:** Clients should arrive at the designated location on time, where they'll meet their captain. This is a good time to discuss the day’s itinerary and any specific requests or concerns.
Safety Briefing:** Before departure, there will be a safety briefing. Clients will learn about the boat's safety equipment and procedures.
The Fishing Experience: Once underway, the captain will head to the fishing spots. Clients can expect guidance from the crew on using the equipment and techniques to catch the targeted species. Charters often provide all fishing gear, bait, and licences.
Support and Instruction:** For beginners or those looking to improve, the crew will offer instruction and support, helping with baiting hooks, casting, and landing fish.
Relaxation and Enjoyment:** In addition to fishing, clients can enjoy the beauty of the open water and, in many cases, wildlife sightings. It's not just about the catch but also the experience of being at sea.
After the Trip
Return and Dock:** At the end of the fishing trip, the boat will return to the dock. Clients often have the opportunity to take pictures with their catch.
Fish Cleaning and Packaging:** All catch will be cleaned for you by the captain and packaged up. We strongly recommend bringing your own esky with ice packs that can be left in the car to keep the catch cool on the ride home.
Additional Considerations
Weather and Conditions:** Clients should be prepared for the trip to be rescheduled in case of bad weather or sea conditions. We allow return of full deposit if the trip is cancelled/rescheduled.
Flexibility:** Fishing conditions vary, so clients should be open to changing fishing spots or techniques as advised by the captain.
Physical Requirements: Fishing can be physically demanding, and seasickness can be an issue for some. Clients should consider their physical condition and prepare accordingly.
Booking a fishing charter is an adventure that offers the thrill of the catch, the beauty of the sea, and an opportunity to learn from experienced fishermen. With the right preparation and an open mind, clients can expect an enjoyable and memorable experience.
- WEEKEND PRICING - Flat Rate of $1,400 regardless of passenger amount
- The minimum age required is 10years old or above. Individuals under 16 must be accompanied by an adult.

Here you can book in lessons for you and your friends on the available calendar dates.

For discounts on multiple surf lessons and a progressive lesson approach, please see our Package Deals!
Important:
New lesson times will be added to the calendar each week so please check the booking calendar regularly for available times slots.
Download The App / Free Surf Lesson Notifications!
Our classes run every day surf is up and by downloading the Wellington Surf Lessons App you can receive notifications on your phone 2-3 days prior to when we are running classes. This is important as lessons are surf/weather dependant which means we may not have all our lesson times available on the calendar until a few days prior.
Note: If you have booked a surf lesson in advance and the weather conditions are not suitable for surfing we will offer you an alternative day to book.
Cost
$89 / surfer (Includes all equipment!)
For discounts on multiple surf lessons - please see Surf Lesson Packages (For individual surfers only)
Duration
2 Hours
About
Wellington Surf Lesson offer super fun group classes for both beginner through to intermediate level students and cater for students of all ages, from kids as young as 7 years old surfing with their parents through to adults of all ages.
Lessons are progressive so we recommend students take 2-3 beginner lessons alongside some practise rentals then 2-3 intermediate classes.
See Package Deals!
Once you've got your surfing to where it needs to be, you can book a FREE Consultation with one of our instructors on the best equipment to buy based on your current surfing ability and goals.
Classes To Choose From
Beginners Classes (Option 1)
Beginner classes will focus on all the important fundamentals you should know before hitting the water by yourself E.g. beach safety, body positioning, basic pop up techniques, catching waves in the white water and more. After taking a few classes we highly recommend students do some practise rentals to practise by them selves.
Intermediate Classes (Option 2)
Intermediate classes will focus on riding unbroken waves, how to get through the waves properly, correct positioning to catch unbroken waves, how to turn and ride across the wave, advance pop up techniques and much more! These classes are suitable for students who have taken at least 2-3 beginner classes, had some practise by them selves and are feeling confident with their pop up in white water.
Recommended Lesson Plan
The lessons are progressive so we recommend students take the following lesson plan:
x3 beginner lessons alongside some practise rentals
x3 intermediate classes alongside some practise rentals
Private lessons with our expert instructors to fine tune your surfing further
For discounts on multiple surf lessons and a progressive lesson approach, please see our Package Deals!
Whats Included
We use the Surfing NZ Approved Softboards which are easy to balance, paddle, stand & turn on
Super warm C-Skins wetsuits
2 hours of expert instruction from qualified Surfing NZ Instructors
Discounts on boards, wetsuits and accessories at our surf shop called Wellington Surf Co based in Miramar
Extra Accessories
Booties, gloves and hoods are $10 a pair and need to be booked and paid for on arrival. Will be first in first served on available sizes.
Need some individual help during the classes?
If you need some individual help during our group classes, don't hesitate to chat with just one of the team at the start of the lesson about your current surfing experience and what you feel you need help with. We will then give you some individual help during the class to fine tune your surfing.

Get your water-taxi to or from Christmas Village which is located on the Northwest Tramping/Hiking Circuit of Stewart Island
The water-taxi trip to or from this destination enables the passenger to save approximately 2-3 days of walking which can save on carrying food for the long hike, or give your already tired legs a break from the last kilometres. It is the closest hut/point to start a climb of Stewart Island's tallest hill, Mount Anglem - Hananui, if weather allows, spectacular views are met from here.
We can customise departure or return times beyond what is offered on the online calendar, please call us for additional times.
Departure is typically from Golden Bay Wharf
Return from Christmas Village is approximately 45 minutes to just over an hour after departing from Golden Bay Wharf
Please be at the departing location 10 mins prior to departure time.
Please also note that the return trip for the watertaxi is approximately the same distance as going to Bluff (South Island) and half-way back - just over 30 knautical miles. This is why Christmas Village is one our most expensive destinations.

Your Cruise - Your Way... Scenic Adventure You’ll Never Forget
Join us aboard Spirit Junior for a stunning Broadwater Island cruise through the Gold Coast’s most beautiful waterways and island destinations. Your journey begins with a relaxing cruise past the iconic Gold Coast skyline, where city meets sea. Sit back and take in the shimmering views as we make our way toward Wave Break Island, a local favourite for swimming only accessible by boat.

We’ll drop anchor for an hour at Wave Break Island, the perfect spot to enjoy a refreshing swim in calm, crystal-clear waters. Relax on the beach or dive in for a splash — this island paradise is your playground.

##Precis of Queensland cycling rules and safety
RULES
PATHWAYS
Shared pathways
	•	Keep Left, ring bell to warn of passing pedestrians
	•	Cyclists give way to people, slow down
Separate pathways
	•	Cyclists use the side of the pathway indicated by the sign
Bicycle only
	•	For bicycles only
	•	You can use any speed
On-road bicycle lanes.
	•	You must follow all road rules
	•	You are sharing the road with other vehicles
	•	Keep as far left as possible
NO Bicycle zone
	•	You must dismount and walk your bike
DO NOT RIDE IN PUBLIC SQUARES, WALK YOUR BIKE.
RIDING
	•	Keep at two hands on handlebars unless giving signals.
	•	Have one leg on each side of the seat.
	•	Face forward.
	•	To signal RIGHT-TURN, extend arm out horizontally with hand open, palm facing forward. To signal STOP, raise arm with elbow bent at right angle and hand up with palm facing forward.
	•	One person per bike unless the bike is designed as a tandem bike.
	•	Keep two meters from the back of a vehicle when following.
	•	DO NOT ride into the path of a driver or pedestrian.
	•	Keep left at all times.
	•	Do not overtake another vehicle on the left if that vehicle is indicating and turning left.
	•	Do not ride more than two abreast.
	•	If riding beside another rider, ride no more than 1.5m apart.
For a more comprehensive list of rules go to https://www.qld.gov.au/transport/safety/rules/wheeled-devices/bicycle 
IF YOU BREAK THE ROAD RULES YOU MAY BE FINED. THERE IS NO AGE LIMIT FOR BEING FINED.
SAFETY
	•	Wear your helmet and enclosed shoes
	•	Cycle at appropriate speed. 
	•	Go slow when there are people about.
	•	Ring the bell when approaching pedestrians, dogs, etc.
	•	Keep left at all times.
	•	Use appropriate lights and reflectors in low light level situations and at night.

Regeneration and renewal of Sydney's inner-fringe. An insiders tour of Sydney with a two-wheeled, architectural twist.
_______________________
 *All tours led by practising architects.
 *Nominated as one of the world’s top five architecture tours by The Sydney Morning Herald.
 *Nominated as one of the world’s top ten architecture tours by The Guardian UK.
_______________________
4 hours (including coffee break)
________________________
Join us on an architectural exploration of the former working-class suburbs of **Redfern, Surry Hills and Waterloo*. Until recently, these suburbs were associated more with pestilence, poverty and crime than hipster cafe's and bars but over recent decades these neighbourhoods have undergone massive change with a steady influx of squatters, students, artists and other creative types creating a thriving scene. Sure enough, the money, the foodies and the architects soon followed!
Sticking to bike paths, back lanes and quiet streets you will experience Sydney at her rawest and her grooviest. Our route and conversation will be structured around a number of **contemporary projects, contested sites and politically charged themes**. You will discover projects large and small including back-lane renovations, houses, public and cultural buildings, contemporary landscapes and paradigm-bending infill and apartment developments. We will cross political, cultural and economic territory as we discuss the patterns driving change and reveal the new ideas shaping how we live in the private and public realms.
Taking centre stage will be a suite of inspiring projects by local heroes **Neeson Murcutt**, **Collins + Turner**, **SJB**, **Angelo Candalepas**, **John James**, **Ian Moore**, **Raffaello Rosselli** and **Andy Macdonald**.
This tour is no touristic join-the-dots. It's an exploration of a city by stealth that will reveal an altogether different Sydney to the one you may have imagined.
_________________________
Prince Alfred Park & Pool** (outside) 105 Chalmers St, Surry Hills. 5min walk from Central Station.
________________________________
What Else.
 **You will need your own bike**. There are various bike-hire and bike share operators to choose from including Mobike and Lime Electric Bikes.
 If you have a **Gift Card**, enter the code in the next window.
 Please bring your ticket for scanning either printed or on your phone.
 Please arrive at the meeting point **10 minutes prior to tour departure**.
 Tickets are transferrable and cancellable up to 48 hours before the event.
 The route is as safe and quiet as possible, a combination of bicycle paths, pavements, laneways and back streets. However, you will still need to be a reasonably confident cyclist. Gloves are a great idea if its cold, and a sun visor or beanie will fit under your helmet. Sunscreen is also a great idea (don't forget the back of your neck and hands!). Rain coat provided in case of unexpected wet weather.
___________________________________
What if the weather is completely rubbish?
 We will not compromise your safety (and we're not complete sadists) so if it looks like there will be awful weather (and we're not talking a little bit of drizzle) the tour will be cancelled and you will receive a full refund. We require a cell/mobile number as part of your booking and **will contact you at least 90 minutes before the scheduled tour if (and only if) the tour is cancelled.

Further Enquiries.
Email info@sydneyarchitecture.org
___________________________________
SAW is a member of **Guiding Architects**, the international network for high-quality architecture tours.

##Precis of Queensland cycling rules and safety
RULES
PATHWAYS
Shared pathways
	•	Keep Left, ring bell to warn of passing pedestrians
	•	Cyclists give way to people, slow down
Separate pathways
	•	Cyclists use the side of the pathway indicated by the sign
Bicycle only
	•	For bicycles only
	•	You can use any speed
On-road bicycle lanes.
	•	You must follow all road rules
	•	You are sharing the road with other vehicles
	•	Keep as far left as possible
NO Bicycle zone
	•	You must dismount and walk your bike
DO NOT RIDE IN PUBLIC SQUARES, WALK YOUR BIKE.
RIDING
	•	Keep at two hands on handlebars unless giving signals.
	•	Have one leg on each side of the seat.
	•	Face forward.
	•	To signal RIGHT-TURN, extend arm out horizontally with hand open, palm facing forward. To signal STOP, raise arm with elbow bent at right angle and hand up with palm facing forward.
	•	One person per bike unless the bike is designed as a tandem bike.
	•	Keep two meters from the back of a vehicle when following.
	•	DO NOT ride into the path of a driver or pedestrian.
	•	Keep left at all times.
	•	Do not overtake another vehicle on the left if that vehicle is indicating and turning left.
	•	Do not ride more than two abreast.
	•	If riding beside another rider, ride no more than 1.5m apart.
For a more comprehensive list of rules go to https://www.qld.gov.au/transport/safety/rules/wheeled-devices/bicycle 
IF YOU BREAK THE ROAD RULES YOU MAY BE FINED. THERE IS NO AGE LIMIT FOR BEING FINED.
SAFETY
	•	Wear your helmet and enclosed shoes
	•	Cycle at appropriate speed. 
	•	Go slow when there are people about.
	•	Ring the bell when approaching pedestrians, dogs, etc.
	•	Keep left at all times.
	•	Use appropriate lights and reflectors in low light level situations and at night.

memory.
This is an open water adventure.

Embark on an unforgettable self-guided canoe adventure through the heart of Whanganui National Park on New Zealand’s iconic Whanganui River Journey.
This 3 day / 2 night freedom hire experience begins at Whakahoro and finishes at Pipiriki, taking you through remote native forest, dramatic river scenery, historic sites, and one of New Zealand’s most unique Great Journey experiences.
Unlike our accommodation-included package, this option does not include indoor accommodation prior to departure. However, customers are welcome to:

Your River Journey
Your adventure begins with a scenic shuttle from Owhango to the Whakahoro launch point, where you’ll begin paddling downstream through the remote beauty of Whanganui National Park.

One of the highlights of the journey is the famous Bridge to Nowhere walk at Mangapurua Landing — a fascinating remnant of a forgotten farming settlement hidden deep within the forest.
At the conclusion of your journey at Pipiriki, our shuttle will transport you back to Owhango, arriving approximately 2:30pm.

The Whanganui River Journey is one of New Zealand’s Great Walk / Great Journey experiences and offers an incredible balance of adventure, relaxation, scenery, and cultural history.

Heads up BENDIGO!! Get ready for an adrenaline-packed adventure that's about to take your WEEKEND FUN to a whole new level!
Tuff Nutterz is coming to town for the first time ever and you cannot miss it! . Get your heart racing as you conquer the twists, turns, and challenges of Australia's biggest inflatable adventure.
It's the ultimate family day out, where the young and young-at-heart can run, jump, and laugh their way through a whirlwind of fun. Don't miss out on the chance to make unforgettable memories and experience the thrill of Tuff Nutterz at GRIFFITH PARK. So get your tickets, rally your crew, and prepare for an adventure like no other!
What's Tuff Nutterz all about? It's not just about the obstacles; it's about creating unforgettable memories for the whole family! You'll need to climb, slide, jump, and crawl your way to the finish line, all while having a blast with your family and friends.
Why You Can't Miss It - Tuff Nutterz isn't just an event; it's a celebration of togetherness, of pushing boundaries, and of pure, unadulterated fun! Whether you're a thrill-seeker or just looking for a fantastic day out with the family, Tuff Nutterz has something for everyone! With Tuff Nutterz, there's no need to worry about age restrictions because the event welcomes all ages to participate and enjoy the fun. Parents with children under 5 years old are offered a special accompanying parent ticket.
So, gather your family and friends and get ready to tackle Australia's most exciting activity!!
Event dates
13 & 14 September 2025
Opening Hours
9:00 Am - 4:45 Pm
Last entry at 3:00 Pm!
Adress
42 – 72 Holmes Road, North Bendigo, Victoria, 3550
About
We tour the country bringing fun and excitement wherever we go. Some of the most iconic locations we've been to include Centennial Park, Darling Harbour, ICC, Parliamentary Triangle, Byron Bay and many more.
Ages
Suitable for all ages
Under 5’s require an accompanying parent/carer. (Grab our toddler ticket which includes a parent ticket )
Responsible adults MUST remain within the premises for all minors.
Important Ticket Info
We strongly suggest booking online to avoid disappointment.
Each Toddler includes a parent ticket. Purchase the toddler ticket and an extra wristband will be automatically provided when you check-in at the event.
Only participants entering the actual inflatables need tickets. Spectators can remain on the premises without a ticket as long as they are not entering the games.
Group bookings can include toddlers. Hence,  have in mind the number of toddlers so you make sure you are not overbooking. Tick the checkbox if a group rate ticket correspond to a toddler so we can provide an extra ticket upon check in.
What happens if it rains?
We won’t let t rain stop the fun! We recommend you bring a spare set of clothes and towels. Take extra care if surfaces are slippery and wear socks with grip tread soles (You are welcome to re-schedule or request a gift-card if you don't want to participate in the rain).
In the event of thunderstorms, heavy rain/winds or extreme weather conditions that could represent a risk we reserve the right to postpone, reschedule or cancel sessions or the event. We keep a close eye on the weather ahead of our events and will communicate any changes as soon as we can to ticket holders via email.
If an event session/day is cancelled/postponed on account of the weather, customers will be issued a gift card to be used anytime in the future.
What to bring
Socks (preferably grip soles), water bottle (No glass), sunscreen, picnic blanket and some form of shade if needed.
Please bring your booking QR Code and signed online waivers, either on your phone or hard copy to help us speed up the check-in process. Make your way to the ticket office to check in and get your wristbands. You can keep your wristband as a memento.
Storage
Lockers are not available at the event, but you can leave your belongings safely with our staff at the ticket office, at no charge.
Food & Drinks
We will have coffee, ice cream and yummy food available for purchase at our events (availability dependent).
You may bring your own food/drinks too. No alcohol is permitted.
No food or drinks are allowed on or near the inflatables.
No glass is permitted on the premises for safety reasons.
Cancellation Policy
All sales are final, however, bookings can be re-scheduled or cancelled up to 24hs before your booking date. Go to your confirmation email and find "change booking" or "cancel booking" below your booking date and time. Click on it and follow the process to change your booking or to cancel and receive a gift card to rebook at your convenience.
In the case we need to cancel due to bad weather you will automatically receive a gift card to rebook for another day.
Didn't make it? Chill out, no shows will also be issued with a gift card upon request to come back another day.

We require **all visitors who are participating** in any of our activities to **sign a waiver** as, like with any high-intensity activity, it informs you of the risks involved. It also asks for a few things in return from you, as our guests, to keep yourselves, your group, and our staff safe. If participants are under the age of 18, a parent or legal guardian must sign the waiver on their behalf. Please **forward the waiver link to other parents/legal guardians in your group**.

The Waiver is to make sure you:

Understand and agree to abide by our safety rules
Agree to follow any rules or advice from our staff on site
Agree to make sure that any children you are responsible for abiding by our rules
Understand that you, and any children you are responsible for, participate at your own risk

**Once waivers are signed online just bring your booking QR Code either on your phone or hard copy (waivers will link to this) and make your way to the office to check in and get your wristbands. 

Please ensure you allow enough time for the check-in process. We recommend at least 30 minutes before the start of your session.

Late arrivals can join at any time, however, the end of your session will remain the same, as your session booked.

##Rules & Conditions of entry
All participants MUST have a signed waiver before entry.

Under 5’s require an accompanying parent/carer at ALL TIMES.

Adults MUST remain within the premises for all minors.

No food, no shoes, no sharp objects (including keys), no glasses, no glass, no jewellery, no candy, no gum, no mobile phones, no pets, no smoking, no alcohol or drugs or being under the influence of alcohol/drugs/medication.

No running, please take your time, no rushing or rushing others.

Allow plenty of space for the person in front of you.

ALWAYS look up whilst climbing. Do not climb underneath someone climbing above you. People can slip and fall whilst climbing. Use straps while climbing and take one step at a time.

No climbing or hanging from outside walls.

Make sure the landing area is clear of all people before jumping or sliding. Jump ONE at a time.

The correct sliding position on the slides is to have arms crossed across your chest with feet and legs together.

If sliding with another DO NOT hold hands. Slide separately.

Do not slide down any area that has climbing handles attached.

No pushing or rough play.

Smaller children should always be given right of way.

No tumbling or flipping and no diving.

Tread carefully and show caution as the course is uneven and spongy.

The course is only for use during public opening hours when obstacle course staff are on duty.

Obstacle Course staff directions must always be followed.

No medical conditions (Heart conditions, pregnancy, etc).Maximum weight 100Kg.

You may hear a whistle or megaphone announcement meaning stop and listen, wait for instructions in case of an emergency.

Enter at your own risk

If an event session/day is cancelled/postponed on account of the weather, customers will be issued with a gift card to be used anytime in the future.

##Storage
Lockers are not available at the event, but you can leave your belongings at the ticket office with our staff if needed.

##Food & Drinks
We will have coffee, ice cream and yummy food available for purchase at our events.
You may bring your own food/drinks too. No alcohol is permitted.
No food or drinks are allowed on or near the inflatables.

Kayak To Cape Hauy, A Star Feature Of Tasmania’s Newest World-Class Hike - The Three Capes Track
Duration
5-6 Hours
About
Tasmania's (if not Australia's) most spectacular day sea kayaking tour
Get up-close and personal with the southern hemisphere’s highest sea cliffs and resident Australian fur seals.
At sea level you’ll truly appreciate the scale of Australia’s highest sea cliffs, gazing up at 200-metre-high fluted rock formations, peering into natural sea caves, photographing the towering Candlestick, and searching for climbers on the Totem Pole - a sheer column famed amongst thrill-seeking rock climbers.
Enjoy our gourmet Tasmanian lunch at a deserted cove, paddle over a semi-submerged shipwreck and marvel at the abundant marine wildlife that lives along this coast, including resident fur seals, soaring sea eagles, diving gannets, cliff-nesting cormorants, peregrine falcons, and if we’re lucky - a pod of dolphins or a migrating whale.
PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS:
While kayaking experience is not necessary this tour can be physically demanding and you do need to be able to paddle consistently for up to 5 hours (you do get a break for lunch though!). Imagine a road trip so diverse you are snowboarding & surfing in less than 24 hours!
Join WAM on our epic 5 day, 4 night snow & surf adventure along the Great Alpine Road from the awe-inspiring Australian Alps, to the sensational Gippsland Coastline.

Thanks for choosing this Great Alpine & Lakes winter adventure with WAM! We can't wait for you to join us on a spectacular journey into the Victorian Alps and Gippsland Lakes.

Mornington Peninsula
Frankston
Melbourne CBD

- We can help arrange equipment hire and lessons at Mount Hotham if required so please contact us for further details.

- To maximise your comfort we provide you with an eco-pack for the trip which includes products from Australian businesses that directly support the environment. This includes a reusable water bottle, keep-cup, reef-safe sunscreen, sunscreen and a towel. You simply hand these back at the end of your experience. Its a bit like a pack you may get on a first class flight or a luxury hotel, except ours is good for the planet!

##Now for the deep and meaningful:
By booking an adventure with us you have directly helped make a long-term positive environmental and social impact by:

- Donating a portion of everything booking to Zoos Victoria to support the Mountain Pygmy Possum (and other endangered species), these little guys were thought to be extinct until being discovered in a loft in Hotham in the 1960's. Critically endangered, Mountain Pygmy Possums are Australia's only hibernating marsupial so will be sleeping while we are on the slopes above, knowing we have supported the conservation of this very special species. 

- Planting native trees on the Mornington Peninsula with MP Koalas to capture carbon emissions, protect our climate, enhance soil and water quality, and restore habitat for native wildlife. 
- Regenerate reefs and native kelp locally with The Nature Conservancy, providing marine habitat, filtering seawater, removing nitrogen and phosphate, and preventing used shell from entering landfill.
- Support female education with The Stars Foundation which empowers and supports Indigenous young women and girls to complete education and find work.

As members of Australia’s tourism industry, we believe a land as precious

Passed down through story and practice, they’re how we walk gently, listen deeply, tread with care – and look out for each other along the way. 

By following them throughout your visit, you too can care for Australia when you Come and say G’day.

Consider these principles a bit of local knowledge. A few fundamentals to help you respect this place and have an unforgettable stay in the process.

The Guiding Principles:

Celebrate Community
The best part of an Australian visit is the people you meet.
Shop local, engage with communities, and you’ll leave with new mates aplenty.

Embrace Culture
Australia’s cultural diversity stretches from ancient songlines to city laneways. Immerse yourself in it all - honour First Nations cultures, embrace our diversity, and you’ll leave with new knowledge and new friends.

Preserve Place
In Australia you’ll find some of the most unspoilt landscapes on Earth. Help keep them that way by minimising your impact wherever you go.

Respect Wildlife
Australia has some of the most unique animals on the planet. Take as many photos as you like but remember to give them space and respect their homes.

Take Care
We look out for one another in Australia, but it’s important to take care of yourself too. Listen to the land, respect it, and always put safety first.

Nic 'Coops' Cooper
WAM Founder

Packraft Adventure Race Training – DAY COURSE
Designed and tailored for Adventure Race paddlers in packrafts that seek to ensure that they have the knowledge and skills to race safely and competently on any river system.
This is a compressed day course for advanced training:
Advanced paddling techniques:
Go beyond basic strokes to include techniques like ferry gliding, eddy hopping, and breaking in/out of currents efficiently to navigate complex river features.
Water reading and hydrology:
Develop a deeper understanding of how water flows and interacts with the riverbed to make smarter, safer choices during a race.
Swift water rescue and safety:
Master advanced rescue skills, including assisted and self-rescue, throw-bagging, and swift water swimming, which are critical in dynamic race environments.
Risk management:
Learn to assess risks and develop processes for safe river running, including scouting unfamiliar sections, identifying emergency exit points, and carrying appropriate safety and first-aid gear.
Leadership and teamwork:
Develop skills for guiding a team and making decisions under pressure, which is essential for success in team-based adventure races.
Equipment and preparation:
Understand how to use and maintain your packraft and associated gear, including carrying an emergency repair kit.
QUALIFIED GUIDES – LOCAL KNOWLEDGE
Whitewater paddling can be a fast paced, adrenaline pumping experience. So having the confidence and skills to be more agile and to adapt to the dynamic style of paddling that river rapids demand is important.
Exodus Adventures is based where the mighty Nymboida River and Boyd Rivers join force. We have over 35 years of local knowledge and whitewater experience and specialise in whitewater training.
Our whitewater guides are knowledgeable and very experienced and will ensure your day is both fun and safe.
Nymboida River
Our guided training packages will give you the most diverse paddling conditions found anywhere in the world. Explore Australia’s longest-mapped whitewater canoe and kayak trail.
The Nymboida River is also reckoned as a premier river for whitewater and is regarded as one of the best paddling and rafting rivers in Australia. It is also the closest rafting river to Brisbane.
On the Nymboida River you will experience surging grade 1-3 rapids and exciting whitewater. Our whitewater tours will also guide you through deep tranquil pools where you experience the region’s best fauna and flora - you may even see a platypus!
Boyd River

Book now and join our scenic train trip from Drysdale to Queenscliff and return!
Depart Drysdale Station at 10:30am, and sit back as the train works its way though the rugged Bellarine landscape on an unforgettable train journey to the seaside.
Arrival at Queenscliff will be at 11:15am, just in time to find lunch at one of the local eateries, and then explore all the fascinating history that Queenscliff has to offer.

meta_raw_booking_notes:
Dear Patron,

Thank you for booking your journey on The Seaside Explorer, a heritage train experience on the Bellarine Railway. We’re excited to welcome you aboard for a day out by rail — travelling between Drysdale & Queenscliff

**🚂 About Your Experience**

Your adventure begins at your selected Station, where you’ll be greeted by our friendly volunteers in traditional heritage uniforms. Take some time to explore the station and view the beautifully restored train before boarding your carriage.

Once aboard, your train will set off on a 45–55 minute journey through the Bellarine countryside — passing rolling hills, trestle bridges, farmland, and forest, following the Swan Bay shoreline.

At Queenscliff, you’ll have around two hours to explore the seaside town. Enjoy lunch, browse the local shops, or take a walk along the beach before rejoining the train for the relaxing **return trip** to Drysdale.

**🕐 Journey Timetable**

Departs Drysdale: 5:30 PM

Arrives Queenscliff: approximately 6:25 PM

Reboarding at Queenscliff: by 9:20 PM

Departs Queenscliff: 9:30 PM

Arrives Drysdale: approximately 10:25 PM

**Please ensure you are back at Queenscliff Station by 9:20 PM for reboarding.
The return train will depart promptly at 9:30PM, and late passengers cannot be accommodated.**

**🎟️ Ticket Information**

Your booking includes either a return or one-way journey, as selected at the time of purchase.

Return passengers will travel from Drysdale to Queenscliff and back on the same day.

**One-way passengers are responsible for arranging their own transport at the opposite end of the line (Drysdale or Queenscliff).**
Please double-check your ticket details prior to travel to ensure your plans match your booking.

**🔥 Locomotive Information**

The Seaside Explorer may be hauled by either a steam or heritage diesel locomotive, depending on weather and operating conditions. Both are genuine historic engines from our collection, and each provides a unique experience.

**📍 Before You Travel**
Ensure you know your departure location (Selected when tickets were purchased)

Departure point: Drysdale Station, 2-10 Station Street, Drysdale VIC
Departure point: Queenscliff Station, 20 Symonds St, Queenscliff VIC

Please arrive: at least 20 minutes before departure to allow time for boarding

Parking: available at the station

**Return Duration:** approximately 4.5 hours total, including time in Queenscliff
**One-way Duration:** 55mins

**🎟️ Tickets & Boarding**

Your booking details and seating will be confirmed on arrival at the Drysdale Station Office, where you’ll collect your souvenir cardboard ticket before boarding.

We look forward to sharing this special journey with you — a true step back in time aboard the Seaside Explorer.

If you have any questions before the day, please don’t hesitate to contact us at
📧 info@bellarinerailway.com.au or visit www.bellarinerailway.com.au/seaside-explorer

**Please note:
If you have booked a one-way ticket, your fare includes travel in one direction only. There is no return service included, and you will need to arrange your own transport at the end of your journey.**

Kind regards,
The Bellarine Railway Team

**PLANNING YOUR DIVE BUSSELTON JETTY TOUR MEDICAL ISSUES** If you have existing medical issues that may preclude you from diving (asthma, epilepsy, heart condition, diabetes, vertigo, issues etc) you will need to get a Medical Form from your doctor to confirm you are fit and healthy to dive or do an undersea walk. Please bring this with you for your tour. Also attached is a copy of the Participant Record form you will be required to complete to do your dive. START TIME AND WHERE TO MEET FOR YOUR TOUR The start time for your tour is when the tour begins at the Universal Access Platform. Two options for getting to the end of the Jetty: a) walk out from the shore (will take 20-25 minutes, suggest you take water, sunscreen, hat and sunsmart clothing for the walk out.) b) book a train ticket out there online at the Busselton Jetty website www.busseltonjetty.com.au Please note that the Busselton Jetty train tickets will cost extra and you may need to walk back from the end of the Jetty at the end of your tour, depending if your tour finishes in time to catch the train back or if there are spare seats on the train.

**RULES**

PATHWAYS
Shared pathways
	•	Keep Left, ring bell to warn of passing pedestrians
	•	Cyclists give way to people, slow down
Separate pathways
	•	Cyclists use the side of the pathway indicated by the sign
Bicycle only
	•	For bicycles only
	•	You can use any speed
On-road bicycle lanes.
	•	You must follow all road rules
	•	You are sharing the road with other vehicles
	•	Keep as far left as possible
NO Bicycle zone
	•	You must dismount and walk your bike
DO NOT RIDE IN PUBLIC SQUARES, WALK YOUR BIKE.
RIDING
	•	Keep at two hands on handlebars unless giving signals.
	•	Have one leg on each side of the seat.
	•	Face forward.
	•	To signal RIGHT-TURN, extend arm out horizontally with hand open, palm facing forward. To signal STOP, raise arm with elbow bent at right angle and hand up with palm facing forward.
	•	One person per bike unless the bike is designed as a tandem bike.
	•	Keep two meters from the back of a vehicle when following.
	•	DO NOT ride into the path of a driver or pedestrian.
	•	Keep left at all times.
	•	Do not overtake another vehicle on the left if that vehicle is indicating and turning left.
	•	Do not ride more than two abreast.
	•	If riding beside another rider, ride no more than 1.5m apart.
For a more comprehensive list of rules go to https://www.qld.gov.au/transport/safety/rules/wheeled-devices/bicycle 
IF YOU BREAK THE ROAD RULES YOU MAY BE FINED. THERE IS NO AGE LIMIT FOR BEING FINED.
SAFETY
	•	Wear your helmet and enclosed shoes
	•	Cycle at appropriate speed.

meta_raw_booking_notes:
Thank you for booking your Kayak/Paddleboard experience with the Penneshaw Penguin Centre!

We’re excited to have you join us and want to ensure you have a safe and enjoyable time on the water. Please take a moment to read the important information below regarding your booking:

• Booking Times
Please arrive on time, as bookings are scheduled to ensure smooth and efficient service for all guests.

• Collection and Return Point
Kayaks and paddleboards are collected and returned at the Penneshaw Penguin Centre. Kayak trolleys are available to assist with transporting equipment to the beach (approximately 20 metres away).

• Clothing and Belongings
This is a water-based activity, so please dress appropriately for getting wet. A limited number of dry bags are available to borrow; however, you are welcome to bring your own if preferred.

• Safety Briefing and Restricted Areas
Upon collection, our staff will provide a map and indicate areas where kayaking and paddleboarding are not permitted for safety reasons. Please follow all guidance provided.

• Wildlife and Environmental Care
We ask all paddlers to respect local marine life and nearby penguin habitats by keeping a safe distance, avoiding landing in sensitive areas, and never feeding wildlife.

• Life Jackets
In accordance with South Australian marine safety laws, lifejackets must be worn at all times while on the water. We have a wide range of sizes available at the Penneshaw Penguin Centre for collection with your hire equipment, and lifejackets are included in your booking.

• Liability
Participants take part at their own risk. The Penneshaw Penguin Centre accepts no liability for injuries that may occur while using kayaks or paddleboards.

meta_raw_description:
Travel just 1.5 hours west of Sydney to experience nature on a grand scale in the UNESCO World Heritage–listed Blue Mountains. Famous for its towering sandstone cliffs, misty valleys, waterfalls, and lush eucalyptus forests, this iconic region has long been a favourite destination for both locals and visitors.
Upon arrival in the mountains, take in spectacular panoramic views from Echo Point, home to the legendary Three Sisters rock formation. Learn about the area’s rich Aboriginal heritage while enjoying sweeping views across the Jamison Valley.
Continue to Scenic World for an unforgettable experience, where your Unlimited Discovery Pass includes all three signature rides. Descend into the valley on the world’s steepest passenger railway, glide above the rainforest canopy on the cableway, and cross the valley floor on the Skyway with breathtaking views of Katoomba Falls and surrounding cliffs. Enjoy time to explore the sub-tropical rainforest boardwalks at your own pace.
Afterward, stop at Cahill’s Lookout for stunning views over the Megalong Valley, offering a quieter and more peaceful perspective of the Blue Mountains. The tour then continues to the charming village of Leura, where you’ll have free time to enjoy lunch (at your own expense), explore boutique shops, or relax in one of the local cafés.
This half-day experience offers the perfect balance of natural scenery, iconic attractions, and relaxed exploration before returning to Sydney in the afternoon.

For everyone who wants to get wet, this is a trip out into the Jervis Bay Marine Park. We will usually visit two of the bays' many dive site for an hour each, allowing everyone to explore either on or under the water.
Time on Boat
Around 4 Hours
About
This is a trip on a smaller dive boats in the Jervis Bay Marine Park. We cater for all people as best we can depending on conditions. You can be a snorkeler, experienced tech diver or anywhere in between on a general boat dive.
GEAR PICK UP AND CHECK IN:
Unless otherwise arranged, we would like you to meet at our shop at the START TIME ABOVE - 2 Erina Road Huskisson -
This is to collect your rental items and check in.
The boat will depart from MURRAYS BOAT RAMP IN THE BOODEREE NATIONAL PARK around 45 MINUTES to AN HOUR AFTER the START TIME please get to the wharf as soon as possible.
TWO IMPORTANT POINTS
You will need to provide your own transport to Murrays Boat Ramp after check in.
There is $20 fee to enter the Booderee National Park .
On return you can leave directly from the Boat or spend the rest of the day in the park itself there are a number of activities to do within the park, as well as some of the best beaches in the area.
What to Expect
Because of the shape of Jervis Bay, there are dive sites that are sheltered in all but the worst conditions. Average visibility is 10 – 15 meters, and most sites slope down from 5 meters to 30 - 40 meters so you can choose your depth depending on your experience.
We have over 65 Dive Sites with a wide variety of options.
- The northern-most permanent seal colony
- The shark nursery
- Sea caves and caverns
- Governors Wall
- Multiple swim-throughs
- The cleaning station at Elyssa’s Playground
- Whales at the Bluff in winter
To find out more about the critters you can hope to see, check out https://www.divejervisbay.com/our-marine-life
Even though you will receive a Confirmation once booked, we still need a Minimum number of booked divers for the boat to depart and there maybe a possibility we will need to rebook you.
Meet at the Dive Shop at your selected check in time to sign in and kit up.

##✅SSI Registration & MySSI App
To get started, download the **free MySSI app** from the **App Store** or **Google Play.**

You can register **directly through the app** by creating your personal SSI profile. During registration, make sure to:

- **Enter your full details,** including your address
- **Upload a clear profile photo**

👉 Both are required to issue your certification upon course completion.

Once you’ve registered, **SSI will email you a temporary password.** Use this to log in, and then you can update your password within the app.

The app is also where you’ll:

- Access your **Open Water Diver digital learning materials**
- **Log your dives** during and after the course
- Track your certifications and training progress

##🩺 Medical Statement
After registering, go to your profile:
**Personal Data > Training & Documents > Medical Statement & Dive Code**

If you answer "Yes" to any questions on the medical form, you must provide medical clearance from a diving doctor. This applies to anyone who:

- Has a known medical condition
- Is over **45 years old,** or
- Has a **BMI over 30** *and* a **waist circumference** over 102 cm (males) or 88 cm (females)

👉 If required, you’ll need to complete an **AS4005.1 diving medical.** This usually takes around 45 minutes and costs approx. $140–$180.

**Gold Coast Dive Centre**
2/54–56 Paradise Ave, Miami QLD

Free all-day street parking is available on Paradise Ave.

Due to light rail construction and ongoing roadworks on the Gold Coast Highway, parking may be limited on busy days. We recommend allowing some extra time to find a spot and arrive on time for check-in.

The Open Water Diver Course runs over **three consecutive days — typically Friday, Saturday, and Sunday.**

Before your course begins, complete **5–6 hours of online learning** through your MySSI profile:

👉 Navigate to **Training > SSI Open Water Diver Program**

**Day 1 | Approx 6:45 AM - 4:30 PM** **(*Full day*)**
- Meet & Greet
- Classroom session (including written exam)

---

**Day 2 | Two Open Water Dives** **(*max depth 12 metres*)**
- Timing depends on tide & weather conditions
- Followed by dive debrief and logging

---

**Day 3 | Two Open Water Dives** **(*max depth 18 metres*)**
- Timing depends on tide & weather conditions
- Followed by dive debrief and logging

- **SSI Professional Instructor**
- **Full day of pool training**

- All required scuba gear (if needed)

To meet course requirements, you’ll need to demonstrate basic swimming ability:
- **200m swim** (no time limit, any stroke)
- **10-minute survival float**

- Sunscreen, hat, and sunglasses

##Precis of Queensland cycling rules and safety

**RULES**

PATHWAYS
Shared pathways
	•	Keep Left, ring bell to warn of passing pedestrians
	•	Cyclists give way to people, slow down
Separate pathways
	•	Cyclists use the side of the pathway indicated by the sign
Bicycle only
	•	For bicycles only
	•	You can use any speed
On-road bicycle lanes.
	•	You must follow all road rules
	•	You are sharing the road with other vehicles
	•	Keep as far left as possible
NO Bicycle zone
	•	You must dismount and walk your bike
DO NOT RIDE IN PUBLIC SQUARES, WALK YOUR BIKE.
RIDING
	•	Keep at two hands on handlebars unless giving signals.
	•	Have one leg on each side of the seat.
	•	Face forward.
	•	To signal RIGHT-TURN, extend arm out horizontally with hand open, palm facing forward. To signal STOP, raise arm with elbow bent at right angle and hand up with palm facing forward.
	•	One person per bike unless the bike is designed as a tandem bike.
	•	Keep two meters from the back of a vehicle when following.
	•	DO NOT ride into the path of a driver or pedestrian.
	•	Keep left at all times.
	•	Do not overtake another vehicle on the left if that vehicle is indicating and turning left.
	•	Do not ride more than two abreast.
	•	If riding beside another rider, ride no more than 1.5m apart.
For a more comprehensive list of rules go to https://www.qld.gov.au/transport/safety/rules/wheeled-devices/bicycle 
IF YOU BREAK THE ROAD RULES YOU MAY BE FINED. THERE IS NO AGE LIMIT FOR BEING FINED.
SAFETY
	•	Wear your helmet and enclosed shoes
	•	Cycle at appropriate speed. 
	•	Go slow when there are people about.
	•	Ring the bell when approaching pedestrians, dogs, etc.
	•	Keep left at all times.
	•	Use appropriate lights and reflectors in low light level situations and at night.

Under 5’s require an accompanying parent/carer at ALL TIMES.

Adults MUST remain within the premises for all minors.

The correct sliding position on the slides is to have arms crossed across your chest with feet and legs together.

We require **all visitors who are participating** in any of our activities to **sign a waiver** as, like with any high-intensity activity, it informs you of the risks involved. It also asks for a few things in return from you, as our guests, to keep yourselves, your group, and our staff safe. If participants are under the age of 18, a parent or legal guardian must sign the waiver on their behalf. Please **forward the waiver link to other parents/legal guardians in your group**.

The Waiver is to make sure you:

Understand and agree to abide by our safety rules
Agree to follow any rules or advice from our staff on site
Agree to make sure that any children you are responsible for abiding by our rules
Understand that you, and any children you are responsible for, participate at your own risk

**Once waivers are signed online just bring your booking QR Code either on your phone or hard copy (waivers will link to this) and make your way to the office to check in and get your wristbands. 

Please ensure you allow enough time for the check-in process. We recommend at least 30 minutes before the start of your session.

Late arrivals can join at any time, however, the end of your session will remain the same, as your session booked.

##Rules & Conditions of entry
All participants MUST have a signed waiver before entry.

Under 5’s require an accompanying parent/carer at ALL TIMES.

Adults MUST remain within the premises for all minors.

No food, no shoes, no sharp objects (including keys), no glasses, no glass, no jewellery, no candy, no gum, no mobile phones, no pets, no smoking, no alcohol or drugs or being under the influence of alcohol/drugs/medication.

No running, please take your time, no rushing or rushing others.

Allow plenty of space for the person in front of you.

ALWAYS look up whilst climbing. Do not climb underneath someone climbing above you. People can slip and fall whilst climbing. Use straps while climbing and take one step at a time.

No climbing or hanging from outside walls.

Make sure the landing area is clear of all people before jumping or sliding. Jump ONE at a time.

The correct sliding position on the slides is to have arms crossed across your chest with feet and legs together.

If sliding with another DO NOT hold hands. Slide separately.

Do not slide down any area that has climbing handles attached.

No pushing or rough play.

Smaller children should always be given right of way.

No tumbling or flipping and no diving.

Tread carefully and show caution as the course is uneven and spongy.

The course is only for use during public opening hours when obstacle course staff are on duty.

Obstacle Course staff directions must always be followed.

No medical conditions (Heart conditions, pregnancy, etc).Maximum weight 100Kg.

You may hear a whistle or megaphone announcement meaning stop and listen, wait for instructions in case of an emergency.

Enter at your own risk

##What to bring
Socks (preferably grip soles), water bottle (No glass), sunscreen, picnic blanket and some form of shade if needed.

Please bring your QR Code and signed online waivers, either on your phone or hard copy. Make your way to the ticket office to check in and get your wristbands. You can keep your wristband as a memento.

##What happens if it rains?

We won’t let wind or light rain stop the fun! For light rain, we recommend you bring a spare set of clothes. 
Take extra care if surfaces are slippery for instance due to the weather. It is recommended to wear socks with grip tread soles.
In the event of thunderstorms, heavy rain/winds or extreme weather conditions that could represent a risk we reserve the right to postpone, reschedule or cancel sessions or the event. We keep a close eye on the weather ahead of our events and will communicate any changes as soon as we can to ticket holders via email.
If an event session/day is cancelled/postponed on account of the weather, customers will be issued with a gift card to be used anytime in the future.

##Storage
Lockers are not available at the event, but you can leave your belongings at the ticket office with our staff if needed.

##Food & Drinks
We will have coffee, ice cream and yummy food available for purchase at our events.
You may bring your own food/drinks too. No alcohol is permitted.
No food or drinks are allowed on or near the inflatables. 
No glass is permitted on the premises for safety reasons.

##Check in
Please bring your QR Code and signed online waivers, either on your phone or hard copy. Make your way to the office to check in and get your wristbands. You can keep your wristband as a memento.
Please ensure you allow enough time for the check-in process. We recommend at least 30 minutes before the start of your session.
Late arrivals can join at any time, however, the end of your session will remain the same, as your session booked.

##Change of booking
Go to your confirmation email and find "change booking" below your booking date and time. Click on it and follow the process to change your booking.

meta_raw_description:
Discover one of Hobart's classic mountain bike adventures with a self-guided ride from The Springs on Mt Wellington to South Hobart.
This 11km+ ride is a sequence of intermediate descending trails that traverse the north face of the mountain.
Starting 720m above sea level, you'll descend more than 550 vertical metres through some of Mt Wellington's most beautiful riding terrain.
There are a few climbs on this ride, mostly on fire trails that connect the descending trails.
Choose a premium dual-suspension mountain bike or e-mountain bike and ride at your own pace.
These sanctioned trails are signed, though we recommend having a phone app like Trailforks to help with navigation.
Ideal for intermediate riders looking for a flexible, self-guided adventure.

• Please call us if you are running late.

**GETTING TO OUR SHOP**
• Our shop is a 6-minute drive or 25-minute walk from the Hobart city centre.

**PARKING**
• You can usually find free on-street parking on nearby Washington St or Wentworth St.

• Next door to our shop is Ginger Brown Cafe; great coffee, breakfast, and lunch.

• Check the weather forecast and dress appropriately.
• Wear comfortable active clothing suitable for riding.
• We provide riding gloves, or bring your own.
• We provide half-shell rider helmets, or bring your own.
• If you don't have riding shoes, sturdy outdoor shoes are fine with covered toes.
• If wet weather is possible, bring a lightweight rain jacket.
• On wet days, consider bringing spare clothes for after the ride.

**BRING**
• A lightweight backpack (really useful for carrying extra gear).
• Mobile phone
• Snack and drink (bikes are fitted with a bottle cage)
• Sunblock, personal medication.

There are trail maps and navigation notes on our website (see link below).

[www.tasmba.com.au/rideplan-springs-cascades](https://www.tasmba.com.au/rideplan-springs-cascades)

Personal Growth, Lasting Change
River Wellness is an active learning program engineered to build functional capacity, emotional resilience, and independent living skills in teens. Staged in a supportive, remote outdoor environment, this program serves as a powerful circuit breaker for teens experiencing screen dependency, academic burnout, anxiety, or social isolation.
By blending structured Cognitive Behavioural Therapy (CBT) with active paddle training, participants transition into a permanent state of self-regulation, deep confidence, and independent problem-solving.

• Expedition Dates: 7 – 11 October 2026 (Private group departures can be arranged for custom cohorts upon request).
• Target Cohort: Explicitly structured for teens aged 16 to 19.

• Total Investment: $1,430.00 per participant — only $286 pp per day all-inclusive (all meals, camping gear, premium equipment, and therapeutic oversight).
• NDIS Funding Alignment: 100% compatible with Capacity Building funding lines (Development of Daily Living and Life Skills / Increased Social & Community Participation). Itemised quotes are rapidly issued for Plan Managers.
• Skill Requisites: No prior outdoor experience required. Full comprehensive water skills, technical safety briefings, and equipment training are completely provided.
What Your Teen Will Gain: 7 Core Competencies
By booking into this program, participants achieve measurable, practical growth across emotional, mental, and social frameworks:
Nervous System Self-Regulation: Participants learn to transition out of chronic stress or hyper-arousal, lowering baseline anxiety and stabilising emotional volatility.
Digital Independence & Cognitive Rest: A complete screen-free detox interrupts reward-seeking loop dependencies, directly restoring concentration, organic sleep cycles, and focused patience.
Autonomous Self-Belief: Overcoming real, tangible milestones on the water dismantles low self-esteem, replacing it with an internalised knowledge of personal capability.
Canoe Navigation and Internal Locus of Control: Canoe navigation provides immediate feedback, proving to the participant that their deliberate, independent actions dictate their direct path in life.
Adaptive Cognitive Flexibility: Exposure to dynamic natural environments breaks down rigid behavioural patterns, teaching participants how to safely pivot when plans change.
Transferable Grounding Habits: Teens are equipped with portable, real-time stress-reduction breathing techniques designed to be independently deployed during at-home triggers (exams, conflicts, transitions).
Interpersonal & Cooperative Competence: Operating in 1:1 tandem canoe partnerships requires clear boundary-setting, assertive communication, active listening, and collaborative conflict resolution.
The Therapeutic Blueprint: Our 5 Clinical Tools
We utilise the river and wilderness space as an experiential classroom to deliver manualised, evidence-based psychological strategies:
CBT Cognitive Restructuring (Mindset Shifts): Teens learn to identify automated, anxiety-driven internal loops during technical tasks, rewriting unhelpful core beliefs on-site to restore clear logic and action.
Physiological De-Arousal (Instant Calm): Enforced "3-Minute Paddle Rests" teach participants how to systematically lower their heart rate and clear adrenaline via targeted breath work during active tasks.
Isomorphic Metaphorical Framing: Connecting the physical challenges of the expedition directly to domestic life, transforming an on-river action into a profound, memorable lesson for home challenges.
Bilateral Somatic Grounding: Utilising repetitive, rhythmic physical activities - like paddling or hiking - to lower deep neurological stress and ground the autonomic nervous system.
CBT Parallel Processing: Using shoulder-to-shoulder nature environments and shared river navigation to facilitate therapeutic cognitive processing without the confronting pressure of traditional face-to-face evaluations.

Monkey Mia Marine Life Cruise – Explore Shark Bay’s Marine Wonders
Join us on the Monkey Mia Marine Life Cruise and experience the breathtaking beauty of Shark Bay, a UNESCO World Heritage Site. Step aboard the Aristocat 2 , our 18-metre luxury sailing catamaran, for an unforgettable 2.5-hour journey through nature’s aquarium.
Cruise in search of iconic Australian marine wildlife, including dugongs, sponging dolphins, loggerhead and green turtles, manta rays, and other rare and endangered species.
Cruise Aboard the Aristocat 2
Enjoy unmatched comfort and panoramic views aboard the Aristocat 2. With exclusive licensing to interact with marine life in the Exclusion Zone, we can stop at any moment to maximise your wildlife viewing experience.
This family-friendly, wheelchair-accessible vessel includes:
Multiple marine-life viewing vantage points around the vessel
Comfortable indoor and outdoor all-weather seating
A refreshing saltwater boom-net spa (don’t forget your bathers and towel)
A fully licensed indoor Ocean Lounge Bar
Full wheelchair access throughout the boat, including accessible toilets
Marine Life Sightings
Our experienced local crew knows the Shark Bay waters well and will do their best to find and highlight marine wildlife. While sightings can't be guaranteed, each cruise offers a unique and authentic encounter with nature. Wildlife appearances vary by season, with dugong sightings most frequent from August to May.

We suggest bringing camera, sunscreen and sunglasses, as well as bathers and a towel if you wish to join in the ocean salt spa/boom netting at the back of the boat.

Please show proof of booking to the Service staff at the Monkey Mia gate or at the shop on the foreshore.

The skipper and crew have many years of experience in Shark Bay and will always try their hardest to find animals for you to look at. Unfortunately due to seasonal changes our sightings will vary. Dugongs as more prevalent during the months of August through to May and are more challenging during the winter months.

All activities and cruises are subject to weather conditions and at the skipper’s discretion.

These tours will immerse you in the native history of Sydney Harbour and the importance of the land to Australia’s Aboriginal heritage and its significance to the clans of the Eora Nation that once lived where Sydney now stands.
The Aboriginal Cultural Tours extend throughout the six-hectare headland of Barangaroo Reserve, taking in the 75,000 native Australian trees and shrubs that are a feature of the Reserve. As the only public space in Sydney to boast this quota of native flora, this tour is a must for the gardening and green enthusiast.
meta_raw_booking_notes:
# Meeting Point

**Tour groups should assemble at the Munn Street Reserve Entrance. Look out for the 'Official Barangaroo Meeting Point' sign and guides who will be wearing Barangaroo branded shirts.**

# FAQs

**What are my transport/parking options getting to the event?**
Barangaroo Reserve is easily accessible by public transport and on foot from Walsh Bay, Millers Point and The Rocks. The closest stations are Barangaroo Metro, Wynyard and Circular Quay train stations. For further information about getting to Barangaroo visit here.

If driving, there is a 300-space carpark underneath the park, accessed via Towns Place and operated by Wilson Parking. Find details here

**Accessibility**
Barangaroo Reserve is a place for everyone and our aim is to make it accessible to all visitors, of all ages, including those with additional mobility requirements. Learn more here.

**Are there toilets at Barangaroo Reserve?**
Toilets are in two locations within Barangaroo Reserve.

There are toilets inside the heritage 1904 Pump House at Marrinawi Cove, near the Towns Place entrance in Millers Point. Baby change and accessible toilets are located there.

There are toilets, including baby change and accessible toilets, on the ground floor main lobby of the Cutaway. The entrance is at the Hickson Road entrance to Barangaroo Reserve. The Cutaway toilets are accessible via the car park lift or from Wulugul Walk at Nawi Cove. (*Note: Cutaway toilets are currently closed while it is being redeveloped. They will reopen with the Cutaway)

**Is there a cafe at Barangaroo Reserve?**
Not yet. Cafes and bars are open at Barangaroo's southern precinct. It is advisable to pack snacks and bring a drink bottle - drinking fountains are available throughout the park.

**What is the refund policy?**
All sales are final.

**What is your weather policy?**
Tours will proceed in all weather conditions. It is recommended you bring clothing for all weather conditions, including sun, wind and rain protection. In the event of extreme weather such as electrical storms, high winds or extreme heat, tours may be postponed and participants advised accordingly.

**What are the terms of concession tickets?**
Concession tickets require student or pensioner ID cards with a concession ID. Student Concessions are only issued to full-time students – a student ID card does not suffice. Seniors Cards are considered concession cards.

**Whilst photography is welcomed during a tour experience filming or audio recording of tour content without prior consent is strictly prohibited.**

If the houseboat becomes beached and is put into a position whereby it cannot be removed by the tides, your bond will be kept in full and if a second party is required for extraction an extra fee will be issued. If you end your houseboat trip and the vessel is left beached a minimum fee of $250 from your bond will be incurred
